title.zh: 卷二百四十四 列傳第三 宗室一
title.raw: 卷二百四十四 列傳第三 宗室一 Volume 244 Biographies 3: Imperial Clan 1

sentences.zh: 魏王廷美 燕王德昭 秦王德芳 秀王子侢附

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Tingmei; Prince of Yan Dezhao; Prince of Qin Defang; with appended biography of You, son of the Prince of Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Tingmei; Prince of Yan Dezhao; Prince of Qin Defang; with appended biography of You, son of the Prince of Xiu

sentences.zh: 昔周之初興，大封建宗室，及其東遷，晉、鄭有同獎之功。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when Zhou first rose, it greatly enfeoffed the imperial clan; when it moved east, Jin and Zheng had merit equal in reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou dynasty was first established, it enfeoffed members of the royal house on a grand scale; after the capital moved east, the states of Jin and Zheng shared comparable merit in supporting the throne.

sentences.zh: 然其衰也，幹弱而枝強。

translations.literal: Yet in its decline, the trunk was weak while the branches were strong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as the dynasty declined, the central authority grew weak while the regional branches grew strong.

sentences.zh: 後世於是有矯其失者，而封建不復古矣。

translations.literal: Later ages therefore had those who corrected this error, and enfeoffment did not return to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties produced reformers who sought to correct this mistake, and the ancient system of enfeoffment was not revived.

sentences.zh: 宋承唐制，宗王繈褓即裂土而爵之。

translations.literal: Song inherited the Tang system: princes of the imperial clan were enfeoffed and given fiefs while still in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: The Song followed Tang practice: imperial princes were granted titles and territorial fiefs while still in infancy.

sentences.zh: 然名存實亡，無補於事。

translations.literal: Yet the name existed while the substance was gone, of no help to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In name the institution survived, but in substance it was hollow and availed the state nothing.

sentences.zh: 降至疏屬，宗正有籍，玉牒有名，宗學有教，郊祀、明堂，遇國慶典，皆有祿秩。

translations.literal: Descending to more distant kin, the Directorate of the Imperial Clan kept registers, the jade genealogy bore names, the clan school provided instruction, and at suburban sacrifices, the Bright Hall, and national celebrations there were stipends and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Even for more distant collateral lines, the Directorate of the Imperial Clan kept registers, names were recorded in the jade genealogy, the clan school provided instruction, and at suburban sacrifices, Bright Hall rites, and other state celebrations there were stipends and official ranks.

sentences.zh: 所寓州縣，月有廩餼。

translations.literal: In the prefectures and counties where they resided, they received monthly grain allowances.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefectures and counties where they were posted, they received monthly grain rations.

sentences.zh: 至於宗女適人，亦有恩數。

translations.literal: As for imperial clanswomen given in marriage, there were also grants of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clanswomen who married out likewise received marriage grants and other favors.

sentences.zh: 然國祚既長，世代浸遠，恆產豐約，去士庶之家無甚相遠者。

translations.literal: Yet as the dynasty endured long and generations receded, fixed estates waxed and waned, and they differed little from scholar-commoner households.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as the dynasty endured and generations receded, their fixed estates rose and fell until, in wealth and standing, they differed little from ordinary gentry families.

sentences.zh: 靖康之亂，諸王駢首以弊于金人之虐，論者咎其無封建之實，故不獲維城之助焉。

translations.literal: In the disorder of the Jingkang era, the princes were slaughtered in rows under the Jin people's cruelty; critics blamed the lack of real enfeoffment, and so they did not obtain the aid of walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang catastrophe, princes of the blood were slaughtered wholesale under Jin brutality; critics blamed the absence of genuine feudal power, which left the dynasty without the support of regional strongholds.

sentences.zh: 魏王廷美

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Tingmei
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Tingmei

sentences.zh: 魏悼王廷美字文化，本名光美，太平興國初，改今名。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Tingmei, posthumous name Wenhua, original name Guangmei; at the beginning of Taiping Xingguo his present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingmei, Prince of Wei with the posthumous epithet Wenhua, was originally named Guangmei; at the opening of the Taiping Xingguo era he received his present name.

sentences.zh: 太祖兄弟五人：兄光濟，早亡，宋興，追封邕王，改曹王；

translations.literal: Among the Taizu's five brothers: the elder Guangji died early; when Song rose he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yong, then changed to Prince of Cao;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had five brothers in all: the eldest, Guangji, died young; when the Song rose he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yong, later retitled Prince of Cao;

sentences.zh: 弟光義，即太宗；

translations.literal: the younger Guangyi, who was Taizong;
translations.idiomatic: the younger brother Guangyi, who became Emperor Taizong;

sentences.zh: 次廷美；

translations.literal: next Tingmei;
translations.idiomatic: next came Tingmei;

sentences.zh: 次光贊，幼亡，追封夔王，改岐王。

translations.literal: next Guangzan, who died young and was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Kui, then changed to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: then Guangzan, who died in childhood and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Kui, later retitled Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，或告秦王廷美驕恣，將有陰謀竊發。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, someone reported that Prince of Qin Tingmei was arrogant and willful and would secretly launch a plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year, informants reported that Prince of Qin Tingmei had grown arrogant and defiant and was plotting a secret uprising.

sentences.zh: 上不忍暴其事，遂罷廷美開封尹，授西京留守，賜襲衣、通犀帶，錢千萬緡，絹、彩各萬匹，銀萬兩，西京甲第一區。

translations.literal: The emperor could not bear to expose the matter openly; he therefore removed Tingmei as Director of the Kaifeng Metropolitan Prefecture, appointed him Western Capital Administrator, and bestowed court robes, a rhinoceros-horn belt, ten million strings of cash, ten thousand bolts each of silk and colored silks, ten thousand taels of silver, and one first-rank mansion in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to expose the affair openly, the emperor removed Tingmei as metropolitan prefect of Kaifeng and appointed him administrator of the Western Capital, granting court robes, a rhinoceros-horn belt, ten million strings of cash, ten thousand bolts each of plain and colored silks, ten thousand taels of silver, and a first-rank residence in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔樞密使曹彬餞廷美于瓊林苑。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Councilor Cao Bin to see Tingmei off at the Qionglintan Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Grand Councilor Cao Bin to host a farewell banquet for Tingmei at the Qionglintan Garden.

sentences.zh: 乙太常博士王遹判河南府事，開封府判官閻矩判留守事。

translations.literal: On the day yi, the Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Sui was assigned to judge Henan Prefecture affairs, and Kaifeng Prefecture judge Yan Ju was assigned to judge the administrator's office.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yi, Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Wang Sui was assigned to oversee Henan prefectural affairs, and Kaifeng prefectural judge Yan Ju was assigned to serve as acting administrator.

sentences.zh: 以如京使柴禹錫為宣徽北院使兼樞密副使，楊守一為東上閣門使充馮樞密都承旨，賞其苦廷美陰謀功也。

translations.literal: The envoy to the capital Chai Yuxi was made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Vice Grand Councilor; Yang Shouyi was made Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and Acting Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs of Feng Prefecture, rewarding their labor in exposing Tingmei's secret plot.
translations.idiomatic: Capital envoy Chai Yuxi was promoted to commissioner of the northern bureau of the palace secretariat and vice grand councilor; Yang Shouyi was made commissioner of the eastern upper gate and acting director of military affairs for Fengzhou—rewards for their role in exposing Tingmei's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍、樞密承旨陳從龍為左衛將軍，皇城使劉知信為右衛將軍，弓箭庫使惠延真為商州長史，禁軍列校皇甫繼明責為汝州馬步軍都指揮使，定人王榮為濮州教練使，皆坐交通廷美及受其燕犒也。

translations.literal: Left Guard General and Bureau of Military Affairs director Chen Conglong was made Left Guard General; Palace Director Liu Zhixin was made Right Guard General; Bow Repository Commissioner Hui Yanzhen was made senior administrator of Shangzhou; forbidden-army commander Huangfu Jiming was demoted to commander of horse and foot in Ruzhou; Ding native Wang Rong was made training commissioner of Puzhou—all for associating with Tingmei and receiving his banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard general and bureau director Chen Conglong was reduced to left guard general; palace director Liu Zhixin was made right guard general; bow repository commissioner Hui Yanzhen was demoted to senior administrator of Shangzhou; forbidden-army commander Huangfu Jiming was demoted to combined horse-and-foot commander in Ruzhou; Wang Rong of Dingzhou was made training commissioner of Puzhou—all punished for ties to Tingmei and for accepting his hospitality.

sentences.zh: 榮未行，或又告榮嘗與廷美親吏狂言：「我不久當得節帥。

translations.literal: Before Rong had departed, someone again reported that Rong had once spoken wildly with Tingmei's intimate clerk, saying, "Before long I shall obtain a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before Rong could leave, another informant said he had once boasted to one of Tingmei's close clerks, "Before long I shall hold a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 」坐削籍，流海島。

translations.literal: " For this he was stripped of register and exiled to the island frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " For this he was struck from the registers and exiled to the maritime frontier.

sentences.zh: 會趙普再相，廉得盧多遜與廷美交通事上聞。

translations.literal: At this time Zhao Pu again became chief councilor and obtained and reported to the throne Lu Duoxun's dealings with Tingmei.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Zhao Pu returned as chief councilor and uncovered Lu Duoxun's dealings with Tingmei, which he reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上怒，責授多遜兵部尚書，下御史獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, demoted Duoxun to Minister of War, and sent him down to the censorial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious: Duoxun was demoted to minister of war and committed to the censorial prison.

sentences.zh: 搏系中書守當官趙白、秦府孔目官閻密、小吏王繼勳、樊德明、趙懷祿、閻懷忠等，命翰林學士承旨李昉、學士扈蒙、衛尉卿崔仁冀、膳部郎中兼御史知雜滕中正雜治之。

translations.literal: They arrested and bound Palace Secretariat duty officer Zhao Bai, Qin mansion clerk Yan Mi, petty clerks Wang Jixun, Fan Deming, Zhao Huailu, Yan Huaizhong, and others, and ordered Hanlin Academician Director Li Fang, Academician Hu Meng, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Renji, and Ministry of Rites director and acting censor-in-chief Teng Zhongzheng to try the case jointly.
translations.idiomatic: They arrested and bound palace secretariat duty officer Zhao Bai, Prince of Qin mansion clerk Yan Mi, petty clerks Wang Jixun, Fan Deming, Zhao Huailu, Yan Huaizhong, and others, and ordered Hanlin director Li Fang, academician Hu Meng, court of imperial sacrifices minister Cui Renji, and ministry of rites director and acting censor-in-chief Teng Zhongzheng to conduct a joint trial.

sentences.zh: 多遜自言：累遣趙白以中書機事密告廷美。

translations.literal: Duoxun himself said he had repeatedly sent Zhao Bai to report secret affairs of the Secretariat to Tingmei.
translations.idiomatic: Duoxun confessed that he had repeatedly sent Zhao Bai to relay secretariat intelligence to Tingmei.

sentences.zh: 去年九月中，又令趙白言於廷美云：「願宮車晏駕，盡力事大王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of last year he again had Zhao Bai say to Tingmei, "I hope the imperial carriage may pass peacefully; I will exert all my strength in serving Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the previous year he again had Zhao Bai tell Tingmei, "I hope the imperial carriage passes in peace; I will devote all my strength to serving Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 」廷美遣樊德明報多遜云：「承旨言正會我意，我亦願宮車早晏駕。

translations.literal: " Tingmei sent Fan Deming to reply to Duoxun, "The Director's words exactly meet my intent; I too hope the imperial carriage passes early.
translations.idiomatic: " Tingmei sent Fan Deming to reply to Duoxun, "The director's words match my intent exactly; I too hope the imperial carriage passes soon.

sentences.zh: 」私遺多遜馬箭等，多遜受之。

translations.literal: " He privately sent Duoxun horses and arrows, which Duoxun accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " He also sent Duoxun horses and arrows in private, which Duoxun accepted.

sentences.zh: 詔文武常參官集議朝堂。

translations.literal: An edict summoned civil and military officials in regular attendance to assemble for deliberation in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned all civil and military officials in regular attendance to deliberate in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 太子太師王溥等七十四人奏：「多遜及廷美顧望兄詛，大逆不道，宜行誅滅，以正刑章。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Wang Pu and seventy-four others memorialized: "Duoxun and Tingmei gazed toward the imperial carriage and cursed it—great treason; they should be executed to rectify the penal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand preceptor of the heir apparent Wang Pu and seventy-four others memorialized: "Duoxun and Tingmei looked toward the imperial carriage and cursed it—an act of supreme treason; they should be put to death to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 趙白等處斬。

translations.literal: Zhao Bai and the others should be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bai and the others should be executed.

sentences.zh: 」詔削奪多遜官爵，並家屬流崖州；

translations.literal: " An edict stripped Duoxun of office and rank and exiled his household to Yazhou;
translations.idiomatic: " An edict stripped Duoxun of office and rank and exiled his entire household to Yazhou;

sentences.zh: 廷美勒歸私第；

translations.literal: Tingmei was compelled to return to his private residence;
translations.idiomatic: Tingmei was confined to his private residence;

sentences.zh: 趙白、閻密、王繼勳、樊德明、趙懷祿、閻懷忠皆斬於都門外，籍其家財。

translations.literal: Zhao Bai, Yan Mi, Wang Jixun, Fan Deming, Zhao Huailu, and Yan Huaizhong were all beheaded outside the capital gate, and their family property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bai, Yan Mi, Wang Jixun, Fan Deming, Zhao Huailu, and Yan Huaizhong were beheaded outside the capital gate, and their estates were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 詔：「秦王廷美男女等宜正名稱，貴州防禦使德恭等仍為皇侄；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The sons and daughters of Prince of Qin Tingmei should receive correct titles; Guizhou defense commissioner Degong and the others remain imperial nephews;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The sons and daughters of Prince of Qin Tingmei shall receive proper titles; Guizhou defense commissioner Degong and the others remain imperial nephews;

sentences.zh: 皇侄女適韓氏去雲陽公主之號；

translations.literal: the imperial clanswoman married to the Han family was removed from the title Princess of Yunyang;
translations.idiomatic: the imperial clanswoman married into the Han family was stripped of the title Princess of Yunyang;

sentences.zh: 右監門將軍韓崇業降為右千牛衛率府率，仍去附馬都尉之號：併發遣西京，就廷美居止。

translations.literal: Right Gate Guard General Han Chongye was reduced to colonel of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard and also stripped of the title Commandant Escort; all were sent to the Western Capital to reside with Tingmei.
translations.idiomatic: Right gate guard general Han Chongye was reduced to colonel of the right thousand-bull guard and stripped of the title commandant escort; all were sent to Luoyang to live with Tingmei.

sentences.zh: 」五月，貶西京留守判官閻矩為涪州司戶參軍，前開封推官孫嶼為融州司戶參軍，皆秦王廷美官屬，坐輔導無狀也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Western Capital administrator's judge Yan Ju was demoted to registry clerk of Fuzhou, and former Kaifeng investigating officer Sun Yu was demoted to registry clerk of Rongzhou—both were Prince of Qin Tingmei's staff, punished for worthless guidance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Western Capital administrator's judge Yan Ju was demoted to registry clerk of Fuzhou and former Kaifeng investigating officer Sun Yu to registry clerk of Rongzhou—both had served Tingmei and were punished for failing to guide him properly.

sentences.zh: 其後，太宗從容謂宰相曰：「廷美母陳國夫人耿氏，朕乳母也，後出嫁趙氏，生廷俊。

translations.literal: Thereafter Taizong spoke at leisure to the chief councilors: "Tingmei's mother, Lady Geng of the State of Chen, was my wet nurse; later she married into the Zhao clan and bore Tingjun.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizong spoke privately to his chief councilors: "Tingmei's mother, Lady Geng of Chen, was my wet nurse; she later married into the Zhao clan and bore Tingjun.

sentences.zh: 朕以廷美故，令廷俊屬鞬左右，而廷俊泄禁中事於廷美。

translations.literal: Because of Tingmei I had Tingjun attend me with sword and shield, yet Tingjun leaked inner-palace affairs to Tingmei.
translations.idiomatic: For Tingmei's sake I kept Tingjun at my side armed with sword and shield, yet he leaked palace secrets to Tingmei.

sentences.zh: 邇者，鑿西池，水心殿成，橋樑未備，朕將泛舟往焉。

translations.literal: Recently, when the West Pool was excavated and the Water-Heart Hall was completed but the bridge was not yet finished, I intended to go boating there.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the West Pool was dredged and the Water-Heart Hall completed though its bridge was unfinished, I planned to go boating there.

sentences.zh: 廷美與左右謀，欲以此時竊發，不果，即詐稱疾于邸，俟朕臨省，因而為變。

translations.literal: Tingmei plotted with his attendants to seize the moment and launch a coup; when this failed he feigned illness at his mansion, waiting for me to visit him in person so he could stage a mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Tingmei plotted with his attendants to strike then; when that failed he feigned illness at his residence, intending to rise in revolt when I came to visit him.

sentences.zh: 有告其事者，若命有司窮究，則廷美罪不容誅。

translations.literal: When someone reported this, had I ordered the authorities to investigate thoroughly, Tingmei's crime would have admitted no sparing.
translations.idiomatic: Once this was reported, a full investigation would have left Tingmei beyond mercy.

sentences.zh: 朕不欲暴揚其醜，及盧多遜交通事發，止令居守西洛。

translations.literal: I did not wish to expose his shame openly; when Lu Duoxun's dealings came to light I only had him remain as administrator in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: I chose not to expose his disgrace publicly; when Lu Duoxun's collusion surfaced I merely sent him to hold office in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 而廷美不悔過，益怨望，出不遜語，始命遷房陵以全宥之。

translations.literal: Yet Tingmei did not repent; he grew more resentful and spoke insolently, so at last I ordered him moved to Fangling to preserve his life in mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tingmei did not repent—he grew more resentful and spoke defiantly—so in the end I ordered him moved to Fangling to spare his life.

sentences.zh: 至於廷俊，亦不加深罪，但從貶宥。

translations.literal: As for Tingjun, I did not deepen his guilt but merely demoted him with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: As for Tingjun, I did not deepen his punishment but merely demoted him with clemency.

sentences.zh: 朕于廷美，蓋無負矣！

translations.literal: Toward Tingmei I have surely been without fault!
translations.idiomatic: In my treatment of Tingmei I have surely done no wrong!

sentences.zh: 」言未訖，為之惻然。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking he was overcome with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished he was overcome with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 李昉對曰：「涪陵悖逆，天下共聞。

translations.literal: Li Fang replied: "The Prince of Fuling was rebellious; all under Heaven have heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang replied: "The Prince of Fuling was treasonous—the whole realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 西池，禁中事，若非陛下季曲宣示，臣等何由知之。」

translations.literal: The West Pool is an inner-palace matter; had Your Majesty not graciously disclosed it in detail, how could we ministers have known?"
translations.idiomatic: The West Pool is an inner-palace affair; had Your Majesty not graciously disclosed it in detail, how could we ministers have known?"

sentences.zh: 初，昭憲太后不豫，命太祖傳位太宗，因顧謂趙普曰：「爾同記吾言，不可違也。

translations.literal: At first, when Empress Dowager Zhaoxian was ill she ordered Taizu to pass the throne to Taizong, and turning to Zhao Pu said, "You likewise record my words; they must not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Empress Dowager Zhaoxian fell ill she charged Taizu to pass the throne to Taizong and, turning to Zhao Pu, said, "You too must record my words—they must not be violated.

sentences.zh: 」命普於榻前為約誓書，普於紙尾書雲「臣普書」，藏之金匱，命謹密宮人掌之。

translations.literal: " She ordered Pu to write a covenant oath at the bedside; Pu wrote at the end of the paper, "Your subject Pu writes," and it was stored in a golden coffer, entrusted to a palace woman charged with secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: " She had Pu draft a covenant oath at her bedside; at the foot of the document he wrote, "Your subject Pu attests," and it was sealed in a golden coffer under the care of a trusted palace woman.

sentences.zh: 或謂昭憲及太祖本意，蓋欲太宗傳之廷美，而廷美復傳之德昭。

translations.literal: Some say that Zhaoxian and Taizu's original intent was that Taizong should pass the throne to Tingmei, and Tingmei in turn to Dezhao.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that Zhaoxian and Taizu originally intended Taizong to pass the throne to Tingmei, and Tingmei in turn to Dezhao.

sentences.zh: 故太宗既立，即令廷美尹開封，德昭實稱皇子。

translations.literal: Therefore, once Taizong had ascended, he immediately made Tingmei metropolitan prefect of Kaifeng, while Dezhao was styled a true imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, once Taizong took the throne he immediately made Tingmei metropolitan prefect of Kaifeng, while Dezhao was styled a true imperial son.

sentences.zh: 德昭不得其死，德芳相繼夭絕，廷美始不自安。

translations.literal: Dezhao died an untimely death; Defang in succession died young; Tingmei then began to feel insecure.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao met an untimely death; Defang too died young in succession; only then did Tingmei begin to feel insecure.

sentences.zh: 已而柴禹錫等告廷美陰謀，上召問普，普對曰：「臣願備樞軸以察奸變。

translations.literal: Soon after, Chai Yuxi and others reported Tingmei's secret plot; the emperor summoned and questioned Pu, and Pu replied, "Your subject wishes to hold the pivot of power to detect treacherous change.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chai Yuxi and others reported Tingmei's conspiracy; the emperor questioned Zhao Pu, who answered, "Your subject wishes to hold the pivot of power so as to detect treachery.

sentences.zh: 」退復密奏：「臣忝舊臣，為權幸所沮。

translations.literal: " He withdrew and again secretly memorialized: "Your subject, though an old minister, was obstructed by men in favor.
translations.idiomatic: " Withdrawing, he secretly memorialized again: "Though an old minister, I was obstructed by favorites.

sentences.zh: 」因言昭憲太后顧命及先朝自朔之事。

translations.literal: " He then spoke of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian's dying charge and matters of the previous court from the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recounted Empress Dowager Zhaoxian's deathbed charge and affairs of the previous reign from the outset.

sentences.zh: 上于宮中訪得普前所上章，併發金匱得誓書，遂大感悟。

translations.literal: The emperor searched the palace and obtained Pu's former memorial, and together with opening the golden coffer and obtaining the covenant oath, was greatly enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor searched the palace, recovered Pu's earlier memorial, and on opening the golden coffer and reading the covenant oath was deeply moved to understanding.

sentences.zh: 召普謂曰：「人誰無過，朕不待五十，已盡知四十九年非矣。

translations.literal: He summoned Pu and said, "Who is without fault? I have not yet reached fifty, yet I already know the wrongs of forty-nine years.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Pu and said, "Who is without fault? Though not yet fifty, I already know the errors of forty-nine years.

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，以普為司徒兼侍中。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai he made Pu Minister of Works and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinhai he appointed Pu minister of works and concurrently palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 他日，太宗嘗以傳國之意訪之趙普，普曰：「太祖已誤，陛下豈容再誤邪？

translations.literal: Another day Taizong once consulted Zhao Pu on the intent of passing the state; Pu said, "Taizu already erred—how can Your Majesty err again?
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Taizong asked Zhao Pu about the succession; Pu said, "Taizu already erred once—how can Your Majesty err again?

sentences.zh: 」於是廷美遂得罪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Tingmei met with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Tingmei was condemned.

sentences.zh: 凡廷美所以遂得罪，普之為也。

translations.literal: In all, it was Pu who brought about Tingmei's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it was Pu who brought about Tingmei's downfall.

sentences.zh: 子十人：德恭、德隆、德彝、德雍、德鈞、德欽、德潤、德文、德願、德存。

translations.literal: Sons, ten: Degong, Delong, Deyi, Deyong, Dejun, Deqin, Derun, Dewen, Deyuan, Decun.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons: Degong, Delong, Deyi, Deyong, Dejun, Deqin, Derun, Dewen, Deyuan, and Decun.

sentences.zh: 故事，皇族封王者物故，則本宮之長封國公，其後以次受封。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a prince of the imperial clan enfeoffed as king died, the eldest of that palace was enfeoffed Duke of the State, and thereafter they received enfeoffment in order.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a titled prince of the blood died, the eldest son of that house was enfeoffed as duke of the state; younger sons received titles in turn thereafter.

sentences.zh: 於是，德鈞子承簡屬最長，襲封徐國公，官至保康軍留後；

translations.literal: At this time Dejun's son Chengjian was eldest by line and inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Xu, reaching the post of military administrator of Baokang Army;
translations.idiomatic: At this time Dejun's son Chengjian was senior in line and inherited the title Duke of Xu, rising to military administrator of Baokang army;

sentences.zh: 贈彰化軍節度使、安定郡王，諡和懿。

translations.literal: posthumously made Military Commissioner of Zhanghua Army and Prince of Anding, posthumous name Heiyi.
translations.idiomatic: posthumously he was made military commissioner of Zhanghua army and Prince of Anding, with the posthumous epithet Heiyi.

sentences.zh: 承簡既薨，德雍子承亮襲封昌國公；

translations.literal: After Chengjian died, Deyong's son Chengliang inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Chang;
translations.idiomatic: After Chengjian's death, Deyong's son Chengliang inherited the title Duke of Chang;

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，拜感德軍節度使，改封榮。

translations.literal: when Shenzong took the throne he was made Military Commissioner of Gande Army and the enfeoffment was changed to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Shenzong acceded he was made military commissioner of Gande army and his fief was retitled Rong.

sentences.zh: 承慶，官至和州團練使卒贈武信軍節度使、循國公。

translations.literal: Chengqing, reaching the post of Regiment Commander of Hezhou, died and was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Wuxin Army and Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing rose to regiment commander of Hezhou; on his death he was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuxin army and Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 子六人，克繼，善楷書，尤工篆隸，宗正薦之，仁宗親臨試，主令監蔡邕古文法寫《論語》、《詩》、《書》；

translations.literal: Six sons; Keji was skilled at regular script and especially expert in seal and clerical scripts; the Directorate of the Imperial Clan recommended him; Renzong personally tested him and ordered the director to supervise copying the Analects, Odes, and Documents in Cai Yong's ancient script method;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons. Keji excelled at regular script and was especially masterly in seal and clerical scripts; the Directorate of the Imperial Clan recommended him; Emperor Renzong tested him in person and ordered the director to supervise copying the Analects, Odes, and Documents in Cai Yong's archaic script method;

sentences.zh: 復詔與朝士分隸《石經》。

translations.literal: he was again ordered to divide the Stone Classics among court scholars for transcription.
translations.idiomatic: he was further ordered to divide transcription of the Stone Classics among court scholars.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「李陽冰，唐室之秀。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Li Yangbing was the fine talent of the Tang house.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Li Yangbing was a jewel of the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 今克繼，朕之陽冰也。

translations.literal: Today Keji is my Li Yangbing.
translations.idiomatic: Today Keji is my Li Yangbing.

sentences.zh: 」訓子弟力學，一門登儒科者十有二人。

translations.literal: " He instructed his sons and younger kin to study diligently; in one household twelve persons passed the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: " He urged his sons and younger kin to study diligently; twelve members of his household passed the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 嘗進所集《廣韻字源》，帝稱善，藏之秘閣。

translations.literal: He once presented his collected Guangyun Character Origins; the emperor praised it and stored it in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented his collected Guangyun Character Origins; the emperor praised it and placed it in the secret archive.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年，以定武軍節度觀察留後卒，贈開府儀同三司、建國公，諡章靖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou he died as military administrator and observation commissioner of Dingwu Army, posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the insignia of the Three Excellencies and Duke of the State of Jian, posthumous name Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanyou he died while serving as military administrator and observation commissioner of Dingwu army; posthumously he was made grand preceptor with the insignia of the three excellencies and Duke of Jian, with the posthumous epithet Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 承壽，終南作坊使，贈德州刺史、武當侯。

translations.literal: Chengshou, ending as commissioner of the Southern Workshop, was posthumously made prefect of Dezhou and Marquis of Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshou ended as commissioner of the southern workshop; posthumously he was made prefect of Dezhou and Marquis of Wudang.

sentences.zh: 子四人，克己，曉音律，嘗作《雅樂圖》樂曲以獻。

translations.literal: Four sons; Keji understood musical pitch and once composed musical pieces in the Elegant Music Diagram to present.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons. Keji understood musical pitch and once composed pieces for the Elegant Music Diagram to present to the throne.

sentences.zh: 侍宴大清樓，進所學虞世南書，賜器加等。

translations.literal: At a banquet in the Great Qing Tower he presented calligraphy he had studied after Yu Shinan and received vessels of higher grade.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Great Qing Tower he presented calligraphy in the manner of Yu Shinan and received gifts of higher rank.

sentences.zh: 終右千牛衛大將軍，贈深州防禦使、饒陽侯。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard, posthumously made defense commissioner of Shenzhou and Marquis of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as grand general of the right thousand-bull guard; posthumously he was made defense commissioner of Shenzhou and Marquis of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 子叔韶字君和，慶曆六年，與諸宗子帝前臨真宗禦書，選第一。

translations.literal: His son Shushao, styled Junhe; in the sixth year of Qingli he copied Emperor Zhenzong's imperial hand before the emperor among the clansmen and was chosen first.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shushao, styled Junhe; in the sixth year of Qingli, among the imperial clansmen copying Emperor Zhenzong's imperial hand before the throne, he was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，進所為文，召試學士院中等，賜進士及第。

translations.literal: In the early Huangyou era he presented his writings; summoned to the Hanlin examination he placed in the middle rank and was granted the jinshi degree with honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huangyou era he presented his writings; summoned to the Hanlin examination he placed in the middle tier and was granted jinshi with honors.

sentences.zh: 自太子右監門率府副率遷右領軍衛將軍，入謝，命坐賜茶。

translations.literal: From Deputy Colonel of the Right Gate Guard he was promoted to General of the Right Lead Guard; entering to give thanks he was ordered to sit and granted tea.
translations.idiomatic: From deputy colonel of the right gate guard he was promoted to general of the right lead guard; when he came to give thanks he was seated and offered tea.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「宗子好學者頗多，獨爾以文章第進士，前此蓋未有也。

translations.literal: Renzong said, "Among the clansmen many love learning, yet you alone advanced by rank in literature through the jinshi examination; before this there had surely been none.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong said, "Many of the imperial clan love learning, yet you alone advanced through the jinshi examination on literary merit; never before had this been done.

sentences.zh: 朕欲天下知屬籍有賢者，宜勿忘所學。

translations.literal: I wish all under Heaven to know that there are worthy men among the registered kin; you must not forget what you have learned.
translations.idiomatic: I wish the realm to know that there are worthy men among the registered kin—do not forget your studies.

sentences.zh: 」叔韶頓首謝，既退，又出《九經》賜之。

translations.literal: " Shushao bowed in thanks; on retiring he was again presented with the Nine Classics.
translations.idiomatic: " Shushao bowed in thanks; on retiring he was again presented with the Nine Classics.

sentences.zh: 遷右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of the right garrison guard.

sentences.zh: 至和中，上書求試煩劇，加領賀州刺史，終和州防禦使，贈鎮東節度觀察留後、會稽郡公。

translations.literal: In the Zhihe era he memorialized asking to be tried in demanding duties; he was additionally made prefect of Hezhou, ending as defense commissioner of Hezhou, posthumously made military administrator and observation commissioner of Zhendong and Duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhihe era he memorialized asking to be tested in demanding office; he was additionally made prefect of Hezhou, ending as defense commissioner of Hezhou; posthumously he was made military administrator and observation commissioner of Zhendong and Duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 克脩字子莊，仁宗為皇子時，得出入禁中侍學，故仁宗待遇殊厚。

translations.literal: Kexiu, styled Zizhuang; when Renzong was still heir apparent he was allowed to enter and leave the forbidden precinct to attend study, so Renzong treated him with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Kexiu, styled Zizhuang; while Renzong was still heir apparent he was permitted to enter and leave the inner palace to study, and Renzong treated him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗禦大清樓召宗室試書，以克脩為善。

translations.literal: The emperor once summoned the imperial clan to the Great Qing Tower to test calligraphy and judged Kexiu superior.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once summoned the imperial clan to the Great Qing Tower for a calligraphy trial and judged Kexiu the best.

sentences.zh: 終右神武軍大將軍、成州團練使，贈同州觀察使、馮翊侯。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand General of the Right Divine Martial Guard and Regiment Commander of Chengzhou, posthumously made observation commissioner of Tongzhou and Marquis of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as grand general of the right divine martial guard and regiment commander of Chengzhou; posthumously he was made observation commissioner of Tongzhou and Marquis of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 子叔充，父早世，異母弟叔瑁甚幼，叔充拊視誨敕成人。

translations.literal: His son Shuchong; his father died early; his younger half-brother Shumao was very young, and Shuchong raised and instructed him to adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuchong: his father died young; his younger half-brother Shumao was still a child, and Shuchong raised and taught him to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 先是，繼母無敘封法，叔充請于朝，詔從之，遂為定制。

translations.literal: Previously there was no statute for enfeoffment of a stepmother; Shuchong petitioned the court, an edict followed his request, and it thereafter became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Previously there was no rule granting titles to stepmothers; Shuchong petitioned the court, an edict approved his request, and this became standing practice.

sentences.zh: 藏書至萬卷。

translations.literal: His book collection reached ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His library held as many as ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子九人，登科者三。

translations.literal: Nine sons; three passed the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons, three of whom passed the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 卒官唐州防禦使，贈崇信軍節度使、尹國公，諡孝齊。

translations.literal: He died in office as defense commissioner of Tangzhou, posthumously made military commissioner of Chongxin Army and Duke of the State of Yin, posthumous name Xiaoqi.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as defense commissioner of Tangzhou; posthumously he was made military commissioner of Chongxin army and Duke of Yin, with the posthumous epithet Xiaoqi.

sentences.zh: 遺表祈任子，有司格不下，子撫之抗章自列，乞如外官法。

translations.literal: In his final memorial he begged that his son be appointed to office; the authorities blocked it and did not approve; his son Fu submitted a memorial on his own behalf asking that the law for outer officials apply.
translations.idiomatic: In his deathbed memorial he asked that his son be given an appointment; the authorities refused; his son Fu memorialized in protest, asking to be treated under the rules applied to ordinary officials.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從其請。

translations.literal: The court granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the request.

sentences.zh: 宗室正任有遺恩自此始。

translations.literal: Bequeathed favor for imperial clansmen in regular appointment began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this case began the practice of posthumous appointment favors for imperial clansmen holding regular office.

sentences.zh: 德隆字日新。

translations.literal: Delong, styled Rixin.
translations.idiomatic: Delong, styled Rixin.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，卒官沂州守，年二十三，贈寧遠軍節度，追封臨沂郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he died in office as defender of Yizhou, age twenty-three; posthumously made military commissioner of Ningyuan Army and enfeoffed Duke of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he died as defender of Yizhou at twenty-three; posthumously he was made military commissioner of Ningyuan army and enfeoffed Duke of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，從其子承訓之請，加贈崇信軍節度、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi, at his son Chengxun's request, he was further posthumously made military commissioner of Chongxin Army and Honorary Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxi, at his son Chengxun's request, he was further posthumously made military commissioner of Chongxin army and honorary grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 承訓官至順州刺史，卒贈深州團練使。

translations.literal: Chengxun reached the post of prefect of Shunzhou; on his death he was posthumously made regiment commander of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun rose to prefect of Shunzhou; on his death he was posthumously made regiment commander of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 德彝字可久，太祖召鞠于宮中。

translations.literal: Deyi, styled Kejiu; Taizu summoned him to be reared in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi, styled Kejiu, was summoned by Taizu to be raised in the palace.

sentences.zh: 德降卒，授右千牛衛大將軍，封長寧郡侯，代兄德隆判沂州，時年十九。

translations.literal: When Delong died, he was appointed Grand General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard and enfeoffed Marquis of Changning; he replaced his elder brother Delong in judging Yizhou at age nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Delong died he was appointed grand general of the right thousand-bull guard and enfeoffed Marquis of Changning; at nineteen he succeeded his elder brother Delong as acting administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 飛蝗入境，吏民請坎瘞火焚之，德彝曰：「上天降災，守臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Locusts entered the prefecture; officials and people asked to bury pits and burn them with fire; Deyi said, "Heaven sends disaster—this is the fault of the guarding minister.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts swarmed the prefecture, officials and commoners proposed digging pits and burning them; Deyi said, "When Heaven sends calamity, the fault lies with the local administrator.

sentences.zh: 」乃責躬引咎，齋戒致禱，既而蝗自殪。

translations.literal: " He therefore blamed himself and accepted guilt, fasted and prayed, and soon the locusts died of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " He took the blame upon himself, fasted, and prayed; before long the locusts died off on their own.

sentences.zh: 儒生乙恕者，郊居肄業，一日，有屍橫捨下，所司捕恕抵獄，將置於法。

translations.literal: A Confucian scholar named Yi Shu lived in the suburbs pursuing his studies; one day a corpse lay across his lodge; the authorities arrested Shu and imprisoned him, about to execute him by law.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar named Yi Shu studied in the suburbs; one day a corpse was found across his lodge, and the authorities arrested him and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 德彝疑其冤，命他司按之無異，因令緩刑以俟。

translations.literal: Deyi doubted his guilt and ordered another office to investigate; finding no difference, he therefore ordered the punishment delayed to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi doubted his guilt and had another office reinvestigate; when the result was unchanged he still ordered execution postponed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，果獲殺人者，恕遂得釋。

translations.literal: Before long the true murderer was indeed captured, and Shu was released.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the real killer was caught and Shu was released.

sentences.zh: 進封郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to enfeoffment as Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，為右監門衛大將軍，遷左武衛大將軍，改封廣平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was made Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, promoted to Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and his enfeoffment changed to Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was made grand general of the right gate guard, then grand general of the left martial guard, and his fief was changed to Guangping.

sentences.zh: 部民詣闕乞留，有詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: The people of his prefecture went to the capital begging that he remain; an edict praised and rewarded this.
translations.idiomatic: People of his district petitioned at court that he be kept in post; an edict commended them.

sentences.zh: 真守初，召還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhen's reign he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhenzong's reign he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，命判滁州，與德恭並留不遣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was ordered to administer Chuzhou and, together with Degong, was detained and not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he was assigned to administer Chuzhou and, with Degong, was kept at court and not dispatched.

sentences.zh: 三年，授徐州刺史，累遷保信軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made prefect of Xuzhou and successively promoted to military administrator and observation commissioner of Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made prefect of Xuzhou and eventually rose to military administrator and observation commissioner of Baoxin army.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上臨奠，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to mourn; court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him in person and suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 贈昭信軍節度使，追封信都郡王，諡安簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously made military commissioner of Zhaoxin Army and enfeoffed Prince of Xindu, posthumous name Anjian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made military commissioner of Zhaoxin army and Prince of Xindu, with the posthumous epithet Anjian.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，改封潁川。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao the enfeoffment was changed to Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao his fief was changed to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 子承謨，前卒；

translations.literal: Sons: Chengmou, who died earlier;
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Chengmou, who died earlier;

sentences.zh: 承矩，終莊宅使，贈博州刺使；

translations.literal: Chengju, ending as commissioner of the Manor Estates, posthumously made prefect of Bozhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chengju, who ended as commissioner of the manor estates and was posthumously made prefect of Bozhou;

sentences.zh: 承勖至供奉官，贈六宅副使；

translations.literal: Chengxu, reaching palace attendant, posthumously made vice commissioner of the Six Residences;
translations.idiomatic: Chengxu, who reached palace attendant and was posthumously made vice commissioner of the six residences;

sentences.zh: 承節、承拱，並西京作坊使；

translations.literal: Chengjie and Chenggong, both commissioners of the Western Capital workshop;
translations.idiomatic: Chengjie and Chenggong, both commissioners of the Western Capital workshop;

sentences.zh: 承街，內殿崇班；

translations.literal: Chengjie, inner palace honored cohort;
translations.idiomatic: Chengjie, inner palace honored cohort;

sentences.zh: 承錫，供奉官。

translations.literal: Chengxi, palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxi, palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 德雍字仲達，淳化初，授右驍衛將軍，曆右羽林、龍武二將軍，累廷蔡州觀察使、咸寧郡公，終天平軍節度觀察留後，贈宣德軍節度、同中書門下平章事，諡康簡。

translations.literal: Deyong, styled Zhongda; at the beginning of Chunhua he was made General of the Right Valiant Cavalry, passed through Right Feathered Forest and Dragon Martial generals, successively reached observation commissioner of Caizhou and Duke of Xianning, ending as military administrator and observation commissioner of Tianping Army, posthumously made military commissioner of Xuande Army and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, posthumous name Kangjian.
translations.idiomatic: Deyong, styled Zhongda; at the opening of Chunhua he was made general of the right valiant cavalry, served as right feathered forest and dragon martial general, rose to observation commissioner of Caizhou and Duke of Xianning, and ended as military administrator and observation commissioner of Tianping army; posthumously he was made military commissioner of Xuande army and grand councilor of the secretariat-chancellery, with the posthumous epithet Kangjian.

sentences.zh: 明道中，追封廣陵郡王。

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the Mingdao era he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 子承睦、承亮。

translations.literal: Sons Chengmu and Chengliang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chengmu and Chengliang.

sentences.zh: 承睦，終左領軍衛大將軍、彭州團練、虔州觀察使、南康侯；

translations.literal: Chengmu, ending as grand general of the Left Lead Guard, regiment commander of Pengzhou, observation commissioner of Qianzhou, and Marquis of Nankang;
translations.idiomatic: Chengmu ended as grand general of the left lead guard, regiment commander of Pengzhou, observation commissioner of Qianzhou, and Marquis of Nankang;

sentences.zh: 承亮，封秦國公，事見上。

translations.literal: Chengliang, enfeoffed Duke of Qin; his affairs are recorded above.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang, enfeoffed Duke of Qin, is treated above.

sentences.zh: 德鈞字子正，性和雅，善書翰，好為篇什。

translations.literal: Dejun, styled Zizheng; his nature was harmonious and refined; he was skilled at calligraphy and fond of composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun, styled Zizheng, was gentle and refined, skilled at calligraphy, and fond of poetry.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，拜右武衛將軍，四遷至右衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was made General of the Right Martial Guard and after four promotions reached General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Chunhua he was made general of the right martial guard and after four promotions reached general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，加右監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde he was made Grand General of the Right Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde he was made grand general of the right gate guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，贈河州觀察使，追封安鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died; posthumously made observation commissioner of Hezhou and enfeoffed Marquis of Anxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died; posthumously he was made observation commissioner of Hezhou and Marquis of Anxiang.

sentences.zh: 時妻亦卒，男女十四人皆幼，上甚嗟悼之。

translations.literal: At the time his wife also died; fourteen sons and daughters were all young; the emperor deeply mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: His wife died at the same time; all fourteen children were still young, and the emperor grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 子承震，早卒；

translations.literal: Son Chengzhen, who died early;
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengzhen died young;

sentences.zh: 承緒，供奉官；

translations.literal: Chengxu, palace attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Chengxu, palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 承偉、承雅、承裔、承鑒、承則，並西京作坊使；

translations.literal: Chengwei, Chengya, Chengyi, Chengjian, and Chengye, all commissioners of the Western Capital workshop;
translations.idiomatic: Chengwei, Chengya, Chengyi, Chengjian, and Chengye, all commissioners of the Western Capital workshop;

sentences.zh: 承裕，禮賓副使；

translations.literal: Chengyu, vice commissioner of Ceremonial Guests;
translations.idiomatic: Chengyu, vice commissioner of ceremonial guests;

sentences.zh: 承翊，內殿崇班；

translations.literal: Chengyi, inner palace honored cohort;
translations.idiomatic: Chengyi, inner palace honored cohort;

sentences.zh: 承簡，襲徐國公；

translations.literal: Chengjian, who inherited the title Duke of Xu;
translations.idiomatic: Chengjian, who inherited the title Duke of Xu;

sentences.zh: 承幹，終懷州防禦使，贈保靜軍節度使、蕭國公，子克敦，嗜經術，以宗正薦，召試中選，賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Chenggan, ending as defense commissioner of Huaizhou, posthumously made military commissioner of Baojing Army and Duke of the State of Xiao; his son Kedun was devoted to the classics, recommended by the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, summoned to examination and selected, and granted three hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggan ended as defense commissioner of Huaizhou; posthumously he was made military commissioner of Baojing army and Duke of Xiao; his son Kedun, devoted to classical learning, was recommended by the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, passed the summoned examination, and received three hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 元豐間，集父承幹遺文以進，神宗嘉之，詔：「承幹父子以藝文儒學名于宗藩，宜有褒勸。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era of Yuanfeng he collected his father Chenggan's posthumous writings and presented them; Shenzong praised this and ordered: "Father and son Chenggan were famed in the imperial clan for literary and Confucian learning; they should receive commendation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era he compiled his father Chenggan's literary remains and presented them; Emperor Shenzong praised this and said, "Father and son were renowned in the imperial clan for literary and Confucian learning and deserve encouragement.

sentences.zh: 」於是追封承幹為東平王，而賜克敦敕書獎諭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Chenggan was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Dongping, and Kedun was granted an imperial letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: " Chenggan was then posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Dongping, and Kedun was granted an imperial letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 以宣州觀察使卒，贈開府儀同三司、和國公。

translations.literal: He died as observation commissioner of Xuanzhou; posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the insignia of the Three Excellencies and Duke of the State of He.
translations.idiomatic: He died as observation commissioner of Xuanzhou; posthumously he was made grand preceptor with the insignia of the three excellencies and Duke of He.

sentences.zh: 德文字子矼，淳化初，授右監門衛將軍，累遷滑州觀察使、馮翊郡公。

translations.literal: Dewen, styled Zigang; at the beginning of Chunhua he was made General of the Right Gate Guard and successively promoted to observation commissioner of Huazhou and Duke of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen, styled Zigang; at the opening of Chunhua he was made general of the right gate guard and rose to observation commissioner of Huazhou and Duke of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 少好學，凡經史百家，手自抄撮，工為辭章。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; of all classics, histories, and the hundred schools he copied extracts by hand and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning; he copied selections from the classics, histories, and all schools by hand and wrote accomplished prose and verse.

sentences.zh: 真宗以其刻勵如諸生，嘗因進見，戲呼之日「五秀才」，宮中由是悉稱之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong, because his diligence resembled that of student scholars, once on an audience jestingly called him "Fifth Xiucai"; within the palace he was thereafter universally so called.
translations.idiomatic: Because his diligence resembled that of student scholars, Zhenzong once jestingly called him "Fifth Xiucai" at an audience, and the palace thereafter used that name for him.

sentences.zh: 德文本廷美第八子，其兄三人早卒，故德文於次為第五也。

translations.literal: Dewen was Tingmei's eighth son; his three elder brothers died early, so among the brothers Dewen ranked fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen was Tingmei's eighth son; three elder brothers died young, so among surviving brothers he ranked fifth.

sentences.zh: 帝封泰山、祀汾陰、幸亳，德文必奏賦頌。

translations.literal: When the emperor enfeoffed Mount Tai, sacrificed at Fenyin, and visited Bo, Dewen always submitted fu and song.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor worshipped at Mount Tai, sacrificed at Fenyin, or visited Bo, Dewen submitted fu and eulogies.

sentences.zh: 帝每賜詩，輒令屬和。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor bestowed poems, he was always ordered to compose matching verses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor granted him poems, he was ordered to compose matching verses.

sentences.zh: 數言願得名士為師友，特命翰林學士楊億與之遊。

translations.literal: He repeatedly said he wished to have famous scholars as teachers and friends; he was specially ordered to associate with Hanlin Academician Yang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked for renowned scholars as teachers and companions; he was specially assigned to study with Hanlin academician Yang Yi.

sentences.zh: 億卒，為詩十章悼之。

translations.literal: When Yi died he composed ten poems mourning him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yi died he wrote ten mourning poems.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，遷橫海軍節度觀察留後，拜昭武軍節度使，易感德、武勝二軍，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era he was promoted to military administrator and observation commissioner of Henghai Army, made military commissioner of Zhaowu Army, exchanged Yide and Wusheng armies, and was made Honorary Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiansheng era he became military administrator and observation commissioner of Henghai army, then military commissioner of Zhaowu army; he exchanged the Yide and Wusheng commands and was made honorary grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗稱為「五相公」而不名。

translations.literal: Renzong once called him "Fifth Prime Duke" without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong called him "Fifth Prime Duke" without using his personal name.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年，宗室王者四人，以德文屬尊且賢，方漢東平王蒼，進封東平郡王，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingli, among four princes of the imperial clan enfeoffed as kings, Dewen was honored as senior and worthy, compared to Liu Cang, Prince of Dongping of Han, and was advanced to Prince of Dongping with concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qingli, of four enfeoffed princes of the blood, Dewen was judged senior and worthy—likened to Liu Cang, Prince of Dongping of Han—and was promoted to Prince of Dongping with concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 德文雖老，嗜學不倦。

translations.literal: Though Dewen was old, he loved learning without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, Dewen never wearied of study.

sentences.zh: 晚被足疾，不能朝。

translations.literal: In his later years he suffered foot ailment and could not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In later life foot disease kept him from court.

sentences.zh: 六年，薨，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 初得疾，仁宗臨視，親調藥飲之。

translations.literal: When he first fell ill Renzong visited him in person and personally mixed medicine for him to drink.
translations.idiomatic: When he first fell ill Renzong visited him and personally prepared medicine for him.

sentences.zh: 及訃聞，復臨哭，贈太尉、中收令、申王，諡恭裕。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived Renzong again came to weep; posthumously made Grand Marshal, Secretariat Director, and Prince of Shen, posthumous name Gongyu.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death came Renzong mourned him again in person; posthumously he was made grand marshal, secretariat director, and Prince of Shen, with the posthumous epithet Gongyu.

sentences.zh: 子六人，承顯，以王后襲封康國公，官至昭化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Six sons; Chengxian, as son of a queen inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Kang, reaching military commissioner of Zhaohua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons. Chengxian, as son of the principal consort, inherited the title Duke of Kang and rose to military commissioner of Zhaohua army.

sentences.zh: 薨，年七十四，贈太尉、樂平郡王。

translations.literal: On his death, age seventy-four; posthumously made Grand Marshal and Prince of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four; posthumously he was made grand marshal and Prince of Leping.

sentences.zh: 德存字安世，九歲授右千牛衛將軍，曆監門，至驍衛。

translations.literal: Decun, styled Anshi; at nine sui he was made General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard, passed through gate guard duties, reaching Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Decun, styled Anshi; at nine he was made general of the right thousand-bull guard, served in the gate guards, and rose to valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從祠泰山，領獎州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the sacrifice at Mount Tai and was made prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Mount Tai sacrifice and was made prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，以恩遷右羽林將軍。

translations.literal: At the Fenyin sacrifice he was promoted by grace to General of the Right Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fenyin sacrifice he was promoted by grace to general of the right feathered forest.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年六月卒，年三十。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, age thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at thirty.

sentences.zh: 贈洮州觀察使，追封洮陽侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously made observation commissioner of Taozhou and enfeoffed Marquis of Taoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made observation commissioner of Taozhou and Marquis of Taoyang.

sentences.zh: 子承衍，禮賓副使。

translations.literal: Son Chengyan, vice commissioner of Ceremonial Guests.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengyan was vice commissioner of ceremonial guests.

sentences.zh: 太祖四子：長滕王德秀，次燕懿王德昭，次舒王德林，次秦康惠王德芳。

translations.literal: Taizu had four sons: the eldest Prince of Teng Dexiu, next Prince of Yan Dexiao, next Prince of Shu Delin, next Prince of Qin Defang.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had four sons: the eldest, Prince of Teng Dexiu; next, Prince of Yan Dexiao; next, Prince of Shu Delin; and last, Prince of Qin Defang.

sentences.zh: 德秀、德林皆早亡，徽宗時，追賜名及王封。

translations.literal: Dexiu and Delin both died early; in Huizong's time posthumous names and princely enfeoffments were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu and Delin both died young; under Emperor Huizong they received posthumous names and princely titles.

sentences.zh: 燕王德昭

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Dezhao
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan Dezhao

sentences.zh: 四年，從征幽州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the campaign against Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he accompanied the campaign against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 軍中嘗夜驚，不知上所在，有謀立德昭者，上聞不悅。

translations.literal: Once in the army there was a night alarm and no one knew where the emperor was; some proposed establishing Dezhao, and when the emperor heard of this he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign the army was alarmed one night; with the emperor's whereabouts unknown, some proposed enthroning Dezhao—the emperor heard of it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及歸，以北征不利，久不行太原之賞。

translations.literal: When they returned, because the northern expedition had not succeeded, rewards for the Taiyuan campaign were long withheld.
translations.idiomatic: After the return, because the northern expedition had failed, rewards for the Taiyuan campaign were long delayed.

sentences.zh: 德昭以為言，上大怒曰：「待汝自為之，賞未晚也！

translations.literal: Dezhao spoke on this; the emperor in great anger said, "Wait until you do it yourself—then rewards will not be too late!
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao spoke up about this; the emperor flared in anger and said, "Wait until you rule yourself—it will not be too late to reward you then!

sentences.zh: 」德昭退而自刎。

translations.literal: " Dezhao withdrew and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Dezhao withdrew and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 上聞驚悔，往抱其屍，大哭曰：「癡兒何至此邪！

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was shocked and remorseful; he went and embraced the corpse, weeping greatly: "Foolish boy—how did it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was shocked and remorseful; he embraced the body and wept, "Foolish child—how could you come to this!

sentences.zh: 」贈中書令，追封魏王，賜諡，後改吳王，又改越王。

translations.literal: " Posthumously made Secretariat Director, enfeoffed Prince of Wei and granted posthumous title; later changed to Prince of Wu, then Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: " Posthumously he was made secretariat director and enfeoffed Prince of Wei with a posthumous epithet; later the title was changed to Prince of Wu, then Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 德昭喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: Dezhao did not show pleasure or anger in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao seldom let pleasure or anger show on his face.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，贈太傅。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded he was posthumously made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，加贈太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing he was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Qianxing he was further posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子五人：惟正，惟吉，惟固，惟忠，惟和。

translations.literal: Five sons: Weizheng, Weiji, Weigu, Weizhong, and Weihe.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Weizheng, Weiji, Weigu, Weizhong, and Weihe.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年，詔封十王之後，以惟忠子從藹襲封潁國公，而惟吉子守巽以冀王后最長，與從藹同封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingli an edict enfeoffed descendants of the ten kings; Weizhong's son Cong'ai inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Ying, while Weiji's son Shouxun, as eldest of the house of Ji, was enfeoffed together with Cong'ai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qingli an edict enfeoffed descendants of the ten founding princes; Weizhong's son Cong'ai inherited the title Duke of Ying, while Weiji's son Shouxun, as senior line of the house of Ji, was enfeoffed alongside him.

sentences.zh: 守巽官至和州防禦使，贈武成軍節度使、楚國公。

translations.literal: Shouxun reached defense commissioner of Hezhou; posthumously made military commissioner of Wucheng Army and Duke of the State of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxun rose to defense commissioner of Hezhou; posthumously he was made military commissioner of Wucheng army and Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 從藹至齊州防禦使，贈武勝軍節度觀察留後、韓國公。

translations.literal: Cong'ai reached defense commissioner of Qizhou; posthumously made military administrator and observation commissioner of Wusheng Army and Duke of the State of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'ai rose to defense commissioner of Qizhou; posthumously he was made military administrator and observation commissioner of Wusheng army and Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 守巽、從藹卒，以惟忠子從信襲封榮國公，官至雄州防禦使，贈保甯軍節度使、楚國公。

translations.literal: After Shouxun and Cong'ai died, Weizhong's son Congxin inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Rong, reaching defense commissioner of Xiongzhou; posthumously made military commissioner of Baoning Army and Duke of the State of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouxun and Cong'ai died, Weizhong's son Congxin inherited the title Duke of Rong, rose to defense commissioner of Xiongzhou, and was posthumously made military commissioner of Baoning army and Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 從信卒，以惟忠之孫、從恪子世規襲封崇國公，官至右龍武大將軍、沂州防禦使以卒。

translations.literal: After Congxin died, Weizhong's grandson Shigui, son of Congke, inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Chong, reaching Grand General of the Right Dragon Martial Guard and defense commissioner of Yizhou at death.
translations.idiomatic: After Congxin's death, Weizhong's grandson Shigui, son of Congke, inherited the title Duke of Chong and died as grand general of the right dragon martial guard and defense commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 守巽子世清，累官茂州防禦使。

translations.literal: Shouxun's son Shiqing successively held the post of defense commissioner of Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxun's son Shiqing rose to defense commissioner of Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 以本宮之長，得封申國公。

translations.literal: As eldest of that palace he was able to be enfeoffed Duke of the State of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: As senior heir of that house he was enfeoffed Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，坐上書請襲曾祖越懿王封不當，奪一官。

translations.literal: In the Xining era he was demoted one rank for memorializing improperly to inherit his great-grandfather's enfeoffment as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xining era he was demoted one rank for improperly petitioning to inherit his great-grandfather's title as Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 既而議者是其說，乃遷越州觀察使，襲封越國公，進會稽郡王，至保信軍留後。

translations.literal: Later deliberators approved his argument; he was then made observation commissioner of Yuezhou, inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Yue, advanced to Prince of Kuaiji, and reached military administrator of Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later deliberators upheld his claim; he was made observation commissioner of Yuezhou, inherited the title Duke of Yue, was advanced to Prince of Kuaiji, and rose to military administrator of Baoxin army.

sentences.zh: 愛諸弟，作棣萼會于邸中。

translations.literal: He loved his younger brothers and held a "Caltrop and Cassia" gathering at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He loved his younger brothers and hosted a "Caltrop and Cassia" fraternity gathering at his residence.

sentences.zh: 會元豐升祔四後，受命告廟，方屬疾，自力就事，未幾薨。

translations.literal: When the four empresses were elevated to joint imperial temple worship in the Yuanfeng era, he received orders to announce the rite at the ancestral temple; he was then ill, yet forced himself to attend to the duty; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng elevation of the four empresses to shared temple worship, he was commissioned to announce the rite at the ancestral temple. Though already ill, he compelled himself to carry out the task and died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 贈安化軍節度使、開府儀同三司、虢王，諡恭安。

translations.literal: Posthumously made military commissioner of Anhua Army, Grand Mentor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Prince of Guo, with posthumous title Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made military commissioner of Anhua army, grand mentor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Prince of Guo, with the posthumous epithet Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 子令廓嗣，元符三年，改今封。

translations.literal: His son Lingkuo succeeded; in the third year of Yuanfu the present enfeoffment was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingkuo succeeded him, and in the third year of Yuanfu the current enfeoffment was altered.

sentences.zh: 世開，從誨子、惟和孫也。

translations.literal: Shikai was the son of Conghui and grandson of Weihe.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai was a son of Conghui and a grandson of Weihe.

sentences.zh: 七八歲，日誦萬言，既長，學問該治。

translations.literal: At seven or eight he recited ten thousand characters a day; when grown his learning was comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: At seven or eight he could recite ten thousand characters a day, and when grown his scholarship was thorough.

sentences.zh: 事後母孝，撫孤侄如己子。

translations.literal: Filial in service to his stepmother, he raised orphaned nephews as his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his stepmother and reared orphaned nephews as if they were his own sons.

sentences.zh: 宮官吳申為御史，薦其學行，命試學士院，累召不赴。

translations.literal: The palace officer Wu Shen, as censor, recommended his scholarship and conduct; he was ordered to take the Hanlin examination but repeatedly was summoned and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The palace officer Wu Shen, serving as censor, recommended his learning and conduct; the court ordered him examined at the Hanlin Academy, but though repeatedly summoned he would not go.

sentences.zh: 神宗褒異之，召對便殿，論事甚眾。

translations.literal: Shenzong praised him as extraordinary, summoned him for audience in the convenient hall, and discussed many matters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong singled him out for praise, summoned him to audience in the side hall, and discussed many affairs with him.

sentences.zh: 時宮僚有缺，不即請，而以他官攝，故私謁公行。

translations.literal: At the time palace staff posts were vacant, yet he did not immediately request them while other offices held them in proxy, so private visits went on openly.
translations.idiomatic: Palace staff positions then stood vacant, yet appointees did not promptly fill them and other officials held the posts in acting capacity, so private lobbying went on openly.

sentences.zh: 宗女當嫁，皆富家大姓以貨取，不復事銓擇。

translations.literal: When imperial clan daughters were to marry, wealthy great clans were taken by payment, and selection by the office ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When clan princesses were to marry, wealthy great surnames secured matches with payments, and official selection no longer took place.

sentences.zh: 世開悉言之，帝嘉納，欲以為宗正，固辭，乃進一官。

translations.literal: Shikai reported all of this in full; the emperor approved and wished to make him director of the great clan court, but he firmly declined and was advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai laid out all of this; the emperor accepted it with approval and wished to appoint him director of the imperial clan directorate, but he firmly declined and was promoted one rank instead.

sentences.zh: 以其所列著為令。

translations.literal: What he had listed and set down was made regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The items he had enumerated were enacted as regulations.

sentences.zh: 官至奉國軍留後。

translations.literal: He reached military administrator of Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to military administrator of Fengguo army.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈開府儀同三司，追封信王，諡獻敏。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Grand Mentor with Three Excellencies honors, enfeoffed Prince of Xin, with posthumous title Xianmin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made grand mentor with Three Excellencies honors, enfeoffed Prince of Xin, and given the posthumous epithet Xianmin.

sentences.zh: 世雄嗣。

translations.literal: Shixiong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 世雄亦從藹子，少力學知名。

translations.literal: Shixiong was also a son of Cong'ai and was known from youth for diligent study.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong was likewise a son of Cong'ai and was known from youth for assiduous study.

sentences.zh: 熙甯中，詔宗子以材能自表見者，官長及學官以名上。

translations.literal: In the Xining era an edict said that clansmen who displayed talent should be recommended by office heads and academic officers by name.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining an edict directed that imperial clansmen who showed ability should be recommended by name by their superiors and school officials.

sentences.zh: 世雄子令鑠在選中。

translations.literal: Shixiong's son Lingshuo was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong's son Lingshuo was among those chosen.

sentences.zh: 嘗請營都宅以處疏屬，立三舍以訓學者。

translations.literal: He once memorialized to establish capital mansions to house distant kin and three dormitories to train scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He once petitioned to build capital residences for distant clansmen and to establish three dormitories to instruct students.

sentences.zh: 詔用其議，置兩京敦宗院，六宮各建學。

translations.literal: The court adopted his proposal, establishing Dunzong Academies at both capitals and building schools in each of the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his plan, establishing Dunzong Academies in both capitals and founding schools in each of the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，以世雄于太祖之宗最為行尊，拜崇信軍節度使，襲安定郡王，知大宗正事。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, as Shixiong was most senior in descent from Taizu among the clan, he was made military commissioner of Chongxin Army, inherited the Prince of Anding enfeoffment, and directed the great clan directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong acceded, Shixiong—most senior in Taizu's line among the clan—was made military commissioner of Chongxin army, inherited the title Prince of Anding, and was appointed director of the great clan directorate.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年薨，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongning he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，追封淄王，諡恭憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously made grand marshal, enfeoffed Prince of Zi, with posthumous title Gongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand marshal, enfeoffed Prince of Zi, and given the posthumous epithet Gongxian.

sentences.zh: 世福襲封。

translations.literal: Shifu inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 惟正，天聖七年，以久病，帝欲尉安之，由保信軍節度觀察留後、樂安郡公特拜建甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: Weizheng, in the seventh year of Tiansheng, had long been ill; the emperor wished to console him and, from military administrator of Baoxin Army and Duke of Le'an commandery, specially made him military commissioner of Jianning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Weizheng, in the seventh year of Tiansheng, had long been ill; wishing to comfort him, the emperor promoted him from military administrator of Baoxin army and Duke of Le'an to military commissioner of Jianning army.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，追封同安郡王，諡僖靖。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made palace attendant, enfeoffed Prince of Tong'an commandery, with posthumous title Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made palace attendant, enfeoffed Prince of Tong'an commandery, with the posthumous epithet Xijing.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟惟忠子從讜為嗣，官至左龍武大將軍、溫州團練使。

translations.literal: Having no sons, his younger brother Weizhong's son Congchan was adopted as heir; he reached left dragon martial grand general and regiment trainer of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, so Weizhong's son Congchan was adopted as heir; Congchan rose to left dragon martial grand general and regiment trainer of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐射殺親事官削官爵，幽之別宅。

translations.literal: He was demoted and stripped of rank and title for shooting dead a marriage-relations official and was confined to a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: For shooting dead a marriage-relations official he was stripped of office and title and confined to a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 從讜少好學，以剛褊廢，遂自剄死。

translations.literal: Congchan loved learning in youth; discarded for stubborn narrowness, he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Congchan had loved learning in youth, but was cast aside for obstinate narrowness and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悼之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈濟州防禦使、濟南侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously made defense commissioner of Jizhou and Marquis of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made defense commissioner of Jizhou and Marquis of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 惟吉字國祥，母鄭國夫人陳氏。

translations.literal: Weiji, styled Guoxiang, was the son of Lady Chen, Madame of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji, styled Guoxiang, was born to Lady Chen, Madame of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 惟吉生甫彌月，太祖命輦至內廷，擇二女媼養視之，或中夜號啼，必自起撫抱。

translations.literal: When Weiji was born not yet a full month old, Taizu ordered a carriage to the inner court, chose two wet nurses to rear him, and if he cried at midnight Taizu himself rose to hold him.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiji was not yet a month old, Taizu had him brought by carriage to the inner court, chose two wet nurses to care for him, and if he wailed in the middle of the night Taizu himself would rise to cradle him.

sentences.zh: 三歲，作弱弓輕矢，植金錢為的，俾之戲射，十發八中，帝甚奇之。

translations.literal: At three he used a light bow and light arrows, with gold coins set up as targets for play-shooting; ten shots hit eight, and the emperor greatly marvelled.
translations.idiomatic: At three he used a small bow and light arrows, with gold coins set up as targets for play; he hit eight of ten shots, and the emperor was astonished.

sentences.zh: 五歲，日讀書誦詩。

translations.literal: At five he daily read books and recited poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At five he read books and recited poetry every day.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗射飛鳶，一發而中，惟吉從旁雀躍，喜甚，帝亦喜，鑄黃金為奇獸、瑞禽賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor once shot at a flying kite and hit it with one release; Weiji leaped beside him for joy, and the emperor was also pleased and cast gold into exotic beasts and auspicious birds as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor shot at a flying kite and brought it down at the first shot, Weiji danced with delight at his side; the emperor was pleased too and had gold cast into exotic beasts and auspicious birds as gifts for him.

sentences.zh: 常乘小乘輿及小鞍鞁馬，命黃門擁抱，出入常從。

translations.literal: He regularly rode a small sedan chair and a pony with a small saddle; eunuchs were ordered to embrace and support him, and he constantly followed in and out.
translations.idiomatic: He often rode in a small palanquin and on a pony with a light saddle, with eunuchs told to hold him, and he was constantly in attendance wherever the emperor went.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，惟吉裁六歲，晝夜哀號，孝章皇后慰諭再三，始進饘粥。

translations.literal: When Taizu died Weiji was only six; day and night he wailed in grief, and Empress Xiaozhang comforted him again and again before he would take thin porridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died Weiji was only six; he wailed day and night in grief until Empress Xiaozhang repeatedly comforted him and he would take thin gruel.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，猶在禁中，日侍中食。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he was still in the palace and daily attended the midday meal.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong acceded he remained in the palace and daily attended the emperor's midday meal.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，始出居東宮，授左監門衛將軍，封平陽郡侯，加左驍衛大將軍，進封安定郡公。
