translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he first moved out to the eastern palace, was appointed left gate guard general, enfeoffed Marquis of Pingyang commandery, made left swift guard grand general, and advanced to Duke of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he first left the palace for the eastern residence, was appointed left gate guard general, enfeoffed Marquis of Pingyang, made left swift guard grand general, and advanced to Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，遷左羽林軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was promoted to left feathered guard grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was promoted to left feathered guard grand general.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，授閬州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was appointed observation commissioner of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was made observation commissioner of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 凡邸第供億，車服賜與，皆與諸王埒，自余王子不得偕也。

translations.literal: Mansion provisions, carriages, robes, and gifts were all equal to those of the other princes, and the remaining princes could not share alike.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions for his residence, carriages, robes, and gifts all matched those of the other princes, privileges the other princes did not share.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，授武信軍節度，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne he was appointed military commissioner of Wuxin Army and made concurrent director of the regular and irregular secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded he was made military commissioner of Wuxin army and appointed concurrent director of the regular and irregular secretariats.

sentences.zh: 時石保吉先為使相，詔惟吉班其上。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Baoji had already been a commissioner with ministerial rank; an edict placed Weiji's precedence above his.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Baoji had already held ministerial rank as commissioner; an edict ranked Weiji above him.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，封泰山，以疾不從行，詔許疾愈馳詣行在。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when Mount Tai was enfeoffed, he was ill and could not follow the procession; an edict permitted him to hurry to the temporary court when recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong Xiangfu, during the Mount Tai enfeoffment rite, illness kept him from the journey; he was permitted to rush to the emperor's camp once he recovered.

sentences.zh: 還頓鄆州，惟吉迎謁，上勞問再三，改感德軍節度。

translations.literal: On the return the court halted at Yanzhou; Weiji came out to meet and pay respects; the emperor inquired after him again and again and changed his appointment to military commissioner of Gande Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey the court paused at Yanzhou; Weiji came out to greet him, and the emperor repeatedly asked after his health before transferring him to military commissioner of Gande army.

sentences.zh: 明年，疾復作，上屢臨省之，親視灼艾，日給禦膳，為營佛事。

translations.literal: The next year his illness recurred; the emperor repeatedly visited him in person, personally watched the moxibustion, daily sent imperial meals, and had Buddhist services performed for him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his illness returned; the emperor visited him repeatedly, personally oversaw cauterization, sent imperial meals daily, and had Buddhist rites performed on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 三年五月薨，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the third year, at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 廢朝五日，贈中書令，追封南陽郡王，諡康孝。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for five days; posthumously made Secretariat Director, enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang commandery, with posthumous title Kangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for five days; he was posthumously made secretariat director, enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang, and given the posthumous epithet Kangxiao.

sentences.zh: 惟吉好學，善屬文，性至孝。

translations.literal: Weiji loved learning, was skilled at composition, and was utterly filial by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji loved learning, wrote well, and was profoundly filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 孝章皇后撫養備至，親為櫛沐。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaozhang nursed him with every care and personally combed and bathed him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaozhang reared him with the utmost care and personally combed his hair and bathed him.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，以太祖孝章畫像、服玩、器用賜惟吉，歲時奠享，哀慕甚至。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping the portraits, garments, playthings, and vessels of Taizu and Xiaozhang were bestowed on Weiji; at the seasons he offered sacrifice, and his grief and longing were extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping the portraits, garments, playthings, and vessels of Taizu and Empress Xiaozhang were given to Weiji; at each season he made offerings, grieving and longing with the deepest devotion.

sentences.zh: 每誦《詩》至《蓼莪篇》，涕泗交下，宗室推其賢孝。

translations.literal: Whenever he recited the Odes and reached "The Thorn-Elms" ode, tears and mucus streamed down, and the clan praised his filial virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he chanted the Odes and came to "The Thorn-Elms," tears streamed down his face, and the imperial clan extolled his filial virtue.

sentences.zh: 雅善草隸飛白，真宗次為七卷，禦制序，命藏秘閣。

translations.literal: He excelled at cursive script, clerical script, and flying-white calligraphy; Zhenzong classified seven volumes, wrote an imperial preface, and ordered them stored in the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in cursive, clerical, and flying-white calligraphy; Zhenzong arranged seven volumes, wrote an imperial preface, and had them deposited in the secret archives.

sentences.zh: 其子守節，以父所書《真草千文》以獻，詔書褒答，仍付史館。

translations.literal: His son Shoujie presented his father's "Thousand Characters in Regular and Cursive Script"; an edict praised him in writing, and it was still handed to the historiography institute.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoujie presented his father's Thousand Characters in Regular and Cursive Script; the emperor answered with a written commendation and had the work sent to the historiography institute.

sentences.zh: 追贈太尉，明道二年封冀王。

translations.literal: Posthumously made grand marshal; in the second year of Mingdao enfeoffed Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand marshal, and in the second year of Mingdao was enfeoffed Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 子守節、守約、守巽、守度、守廉、守康。

translations.literal: Sons: Shoujie, Shouyue, Shouxun, Shoudu, Shoulian, and Shoukang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shoujie, Shouyue, Shouxun, Shoudu, Shoulian, and Shoukang.

sentences.zh: 寧約，終內園使、康州刺史，贈沂州團練使。

translations.literal: Shouyue ended as inner garden commissioner and prefect of Kangzhou; posthumously made regiment trainer of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue rose to inner garden commissioner and prefect of Kangzhou and was posthumously made regiment trainer of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 子世靜、世長。

translations.literal: Sons: Shijing and Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shijing and Shichang.

sentences.zh: 世靜，至左武衛大將軍、均州防禦使，卒贈鎮海軍節度觀察留後、北海郡公。

translations.literal: Shijing reached left martial guard grand general and defense commissioner of Junzhou; on death he was posthumously made military administrator of Zhenhai Army and Duke of Beihai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing rose to left martial guard grand general and defense commissioner of Junzhou; at his death he was posthumously made military administrator of Zhenhai army and Duke of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 世長，終左武衛大將軍、解州防禦使，贈張信軍節度觀察留後、濟陽郡公。

translations.literal: Shichang ended as left martial guard grand general and defense commissioner of Xiezhou; posthumously made military administrator of Zhangxin Army and Duke of Jiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang ended as left martial guard grand general and defense commissioner of Xiezhou and was posthumously made military administrator of Zhangxin army and Duke of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 守巽及其子世清，事見上。

translations.literal: Shouxun and his son Shiqing: their accounts appear above.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxun and his son Shiqing are treated above.

sentences.zh: 守度，終左領軍衛大將軍、英州團練使，贈廣州觀察使、盧江侯。

translations.literal: Shoudu ended as left wing guard grand general and regiment trainer of Yingzhou; posthumously made observation commissioner of Guangzhou and Marquis of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shoudu ended as left wing guard grand general and regiment trainer of Yingzhou and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Guangzhou and Marquis of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 守廉，終供備庫副使，贈內藏庫使。

translations.literal: Shoulian ended as deputy commissioner of the supply preparation bureau; posthumously made commissioner of the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Shoulian ended as deputy commissioner of the supply preparation bureau and was posthumously made commissioner of the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 守康，至供奉官。

translations.literal: Shoukang reached palace offering officer.
translations.idiomatic: Shoukang rose to palace offering officer.

sentences.zh: 惟固字宗幹，本名元扆，太平興國八年，改賜名授左千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: Weigu, styled Zonggan, original name Yuanqi; in the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo his name was changed by grant and he was appointed left thousand-bull guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Weigu, styled Zonggan, was originally named Yuanqi; in the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he was granted a new name and appointed left thousand-bull guard general.

sentences.zh: 是冬卒。

translations.literal: That winter he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter.

sentences.zh: 從恪，累官西染院使，卒，贈磁州刺史、東萊侯。

translations.literal: Congke successively held the post of west dyeing commissioner; on death he was posthumously made prefect of Cizhou and Marquis of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Congke rose to west dyeing commissioner; at his death he was posthumously made prefect of Cizhou and Marquis of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 子世規，襲封崇國公。

translations.literal: His son Shigui inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shigui inherited the title Duke of Chong.

sentences.zh: 從藹，終左衛大將軍、齊州防禦使，贈武勝軍節度觀察留後，追封韓國公。

translations.literal: Cong'ai ended as left guard grand general and defense commissioner of Qizhou; posthumously made military administrator of Wusheng Army and Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'ai ended as left guard grand general and defense commissioner of Qizhou and was posthumously made military administrator of Wusheng army and Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 子世豐，終太子右衛率，追贈進士及第。

translations.literal: His son Shifeng ended as commander of the crown prince's right palace guard; posthumously granted the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shifeng ended as commander of the crown prince's right palace guard and was posthumously granted the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 世准、世雄，並安定郡王。

translations.literal: Shizhun and Shixiong were both Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhun and Shixiong both held the title Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 從信，封榮國公，官至雄州防禦使，贈保甯軍節度使、楚國公，諡安僖。

translations.literal: Congxin was enfeoffed Duke of Rong, reached defense commissioner of Xiongzhou, and was posthumously made military commissioner of Baoning Army, Duke of Chu, with posthumous title Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Congxin was enfeoffed Duke of Rong, rose to defense commissioner of Xiongzhou, and was posthumously made military commissioner of Baoning army and Duke of Chu with the posthumous epithet Anxi.

sentences.zh: 子世福，襲安定郡王。

translations.literal: His son Shifu inherited the Prince of Anding enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shifu inherited the title Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 從秉、從穎、從謹，並禮賓使。

translations.literal: Congbing, Congying, and Congjin were all reception commissioners for tributary envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Congbing, Congying, and Congjin all served as reception commissioners for tributary envoys.

sentences.zh: 從質，內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Congzhi held the inner palace honored rank.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhi held honored rank in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 從讜，出繼惟正。

translations.literal: Congchan was adopted out as heir to Weizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Congchan was given in adoption as heir to Weizheng.

sentences.zh: 惟和雅好學，為詩頗清麗，工筆劄優遊典籍，以禮法自居，宗室推重。

translations.literal: Weihe elegantly loved learning; his poetry was quite pure and clear; he was skilled at brush correspondence and at ease among the classics; he held himself by ritual law, and the clan esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Weihe cultivated learning with refinement; his poetry was lucid and graceful; he wrote excellent letters and moved easily through the classics; he conducted himself by ritual propriety, and the clan held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 嘗和禦制詩，上稱其有理致。

translations.literal: He once harmonized imperial poetry, and the emperor praised him as having reasoned exposition.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed verses in reply to imperial poems, and the emperor praised the reason in his lines.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上謂宰相王旦等曰「惟和好文力學，加之謹願，皇族之秀也，不幸短命！

translations.literal: When he died the emperor said to the chancellor Wang Dan and others, "Weihe loved literature and studied strenuously; moreover he was cautious and respectful—a fine sprig of the imperial house. Alas, an untimely death!
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor told the chancellor Wang Dan and others, "Weihe loved letters and studied hard; moreover he was cautious and respectful—the very flower of the imperial house. What a pity he died young!

sentences.zh: 」嗟悼久之，至於泣下。

translations.literal: " He sighed and mourned for a long time, even to the point of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: " He sighed and grieved for a long while, until he wept.

sentences.zh: 錄其稿二十二軸，上親制序，藏于秘閣。

translations.literal: Twenty-two scrolls of his drafts were copied; the emperor personally wrote a preface and had them stored in the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two scrolls of his drafts were transcribed; the emperor wrote a preface in his own hand and had them placed in the secret archives.

sentences.zh: 子從審、從誨。

translations.literal: Sons: Congshen and Conghui.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Congshen and Conghui.

sentences.zh: 從審，終復州防禦使，贈甯國軍節度觀察留後、宣城郡公。

translations.literal: Congshen ended as defense commissioner of Fuzhou; posthumously made military administrator of Ningguo Army and Duke of Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Congshen ended as defense commissioner of Fuzhou and was posthumously made military administrator of Ningguo army and Duke of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐與人奸除名，已而復官。

translations.literal: He was once punished for adultery and struck from the rolls; afterward his offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was once punished for adultery and removed from the registers, but later his offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 從誨，終左金吾衛大將軍、台州團練使，贈襄州觀察使、襄陽侯。

translations.literal: Conghui ended as left golden crow guard grand general and regiment trainer of Taizhou; posthumously made observation commissioner of Xiangzhou and Marquis of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui ended as left golden crow guard grand general and regiment trainer of Taizhou and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Xiangzhou and Marquis of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 子世開，安定郡王，事見上。

translations.literal: His son Shikai, Prince of Anding: his account appears above.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shikai, Prince of Anding, is treated above.

sentences.zh: 令矼，紹興五年，由邵武軍兵馬都監襲封，授華州觀察使，尋除同知大宗正事。

translations.literal: Lingjiang: in the fifth year of Shaoxing, from military controller of Shaowu Army he inherited the enfeoffment, was appointed observation commissioner of Huazhou, and soon appointed associate director of the great clan directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjiang: in the fifth year of Shaoxing, from troop inspector of Shaowu army he inherited the enfeoffment, was made observation commissioner of Huazhou, and soon appointed associate director of the great clan directorate.

sentences.zh: 逾年薨。

translations.literal: After a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 令ＳＫ字深之。

translations.literal: Lingxun, styled Shenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxun, styled Shenzhi.

sentences.zh: 初，懿王生昌州團練使惟忠，惟忠生楚安僖王從信，從信生益公世逢，世逢生令ＳＫ，授右班殿直，遷東頭供奉官，累監州縣場庫。

translations.literal: Originally Prince Yi bore Changzhou regiment trainer Weizhong; Weizhong bore Chu Anxi Prince Congxin; Congxin bore Duke Yi Shifeng; Shifeng bore Lingxun, who was appointed right palace guard, promoted eastern-head offering officer, and repeatedly supervised county and prefectural depots.
translations.idiomatic: In descent, Prince Yi was father to Changzhou regiment trainer Weizhong; Weizhong to Chu Anxi prince Congxin; Congxin to Duke Yi Shifeng; and Shifeng to Lingxun, who was appointed right palace guard, promoted eastern-head offering officer, and repeatedly supervised county and prefectural storehouses.

sentences.zh: 監司薛昂薦其才，易資承事郎，調潁州簽判，曆綿州通判，累知蜀州、閬州、慶源府，召除衛尉少卿，擢秘閣修撰，再知慶源府。

translations.literal: Supervisor Xue Ang recommended his talent; his capital qualification was exchanged for court gentleman; he was assigned as signing officer of Yingzhou, served as Tongpan of Mianzhou, repeatedly governed Shuzhou, Langzhou, and Qingyuan prefecture, was summoned and made vice minister of the court for imperial carriages, was promoted to Secretariat compiler, and again governed Qingyuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit intendant Xue Ang recommended his ability; he exchanged his capital qualification for court gentleman, was posted as signing officer of Yingzhou, served as acting prefect of Mianzhou, governed in turn Shuzhou, Langzhou, and Qingyuan, was summoned as vice minister of the court for imperial carriages, was promoted to Hanlin compiler, and again governed Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，分西外宗子於泰州，命令ＳＫ知西外宗正事，除禦營使司參贊軍事，挈宗子避地福州，因置司焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan the western outer clansmen were distributed to Taizhou; the court ordered Lingxun to direct the western outer clan directorate, appointed him military advisor on the staff of the imperial camp commissioner, led the clansmen to take refuge in Fuzhou, and there established the office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan western-branch clansmen were assigned to Taizhou; Lingxun was ordered to head the western outer clan directorate, made military advisor on the imperial camp staff, led the clansmen to refuge in Fuzhou, and established the office there.

sentences.zh: 元懿太子薨，帝命令ＳＫ選藝祖後得三四人，寺擢集英殿修撰，知南外宗正。

translations.literal: When Prince Yuanyi died the emperor ordered Lingxun to select three or four descendants of Taizu; soon he was promoted to Hanlin compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and made director of the southern outer clan directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuanyi died the emperor ordered Lingxun to choose three or four descendants of Taizu; he was soon promoted to Hanlin compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and appointed director of the southern outer clan directorate.

sentences.zh: 再選宗子，得伯琮、伯浩養宮中，後選得伯玖，性亦聰惠。

translations.literal: Selecting clan sons again, he obtained Bowan and Bohao to rear in the palace; later he also selected Bojiu, whose nature was likewise clever.
translations.idiomatic: On a further selection of clansmen he obtained Bowan and Bohao to rear in the palace; later he also chose Bojiu, who proved clever by nature as well.

sentences.zh: 高宗喜，轉令ＳＫ知泉州，尋與祠以歸。

translations.literal: Gaozong was pleased and transferred Lingxun to govern Quanzhou; soon he was granted leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was pleased and transferred Lingxun to govern Quanzhou; before long he was granted leave to retire home.

sentences.zh: 令矼薨，令ＳＫ改閬州觀察使，襲封，除同知大宗正事。

translations.literal: When Lingjiang died, Lingxun was changed to observation commissioner of Langzhou, inherited the enfeoffment, and was appointed associate director of the great clan directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingjiang died, Lingxun was made observation commissioner of Langzhou, inherited the enfeoffment, and was appointed associate director of the great clan directorate.

sentences.zh: 逾年，授鎮東軍承宣使，再遷保平軍節度使。

translations.literal: After a year he was appointed imperial commissioner of Zhendong Army; he was promoted again to military commissioner of Baoping Army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed imperial commissioner of Zhendong army and was again promoted to military commissioner of Baoping army.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年薨，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈少師，後追封惠王，諡襄靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Junior Mentor; later posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Hui, with posthumous title Xiangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior mentor, later enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Hui, and given the posthumous epithet Xiangjing.

sentences.zh: 子子遊，官至湖北提刑，用戶部侍郎王俁薦，加直秘閣。

translations.literal: His son Ziyou reached the post of judicial intendant of Hubei; on the recommendation of Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Hou, he was granted direct access to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyou rose to judicial intendant of Hubei; recommended by Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Hou, he was granted direct access to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會建甯節度使士雪刂知南外宗正司，以事去官，言者請擇宗室文臣之廉正者代之，遂以命子遊。

translations.literal: At the time the Jianning military commissioner Shi Fu was director of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Directorate; he left office over a matter, and memorializers asked that an upright literary clansman be chosen to replace him, so Ziyou was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianning military commissioner Shi Fu, who had been directing the Southern Outer Imperial Clan office, left his post over a scandal, critics urged appointing an upright literary clansman in his place, and Ziyou received the commission.

sentences.zh: 西、南外宗官用文臣，自子遊始。

translations.literal: The use of literary officials for the Western and Southern Outer Clan offices began with Ziyou.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian scholar-officials first served the Western and Southern Outer Clan directorates under Ziyou.

sentences.zh: 令詪，字君序，以父任補右班殿直。

translations.literal: Lingjie, courtesy name Junxu, entered office as Right Guard Attendant of the Court through his father's privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjie, whose courtesy name was Junxu, entered service as a Right Guard Attendant of the Court through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 政和中，遷成忠郎，召試，授從事郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era he was promoted to Loyalty-in-Service Gentleman, summoned for examination, and appointed Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe he was promoted to Loyalty-in-Service Gentleman, examined at court, and appointed an attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，以貢士試舍選合格，授宣教郎，調信州永豐縣丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe he passed the tribute-student palace examination and was appointed Promulgating Instruction Gentleman, assigned as assistant magistrate of Yongfeng County in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuanhe he passed the tribute-student palace examination, was made a Promulgating Instruction Gentleman, and posted as assistant magistrate of Yongfeng County in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 中興初，累遷福州運判，兼提點刑獄公事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration he was repeatedly promoted to transport commissioner of Fuzhou, concurrently serving as judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Restoration he rose through transport commissioner of Fuzhou to concurrent judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 秦檜方柄用，安定郡王絕封者十餘年；

translations.literal: Qin Hui then held power, and the enfeoffment of the Prince of Anding had been suspended for more than ten years;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was then in power, and the Prince of Anding line had gone without a new enfeoffment for more than ten years;

sentences.zh: 檜死，次令衿當封，適以事被拘，遂命令詪襲封。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Lingqin was next in line for the enfeoffment, but was just then detained over a matter, so Lingjie was ordered to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death Lingqin should have inherited the title, but he was detained over a legal matter, so Lingjie was ordered to succeed instead.

sentences.zh: 已而令詪以爵遜令衿，乃升令詪秘閣修撰，知台州，移知紹興府，召權戶部侍郎，令嚴、饒二州鑄錢局。

translations.literal: Soon Lingjie yielded the title to Lingqin; he was then promoted to Secretariat Drafter, made prefect of Taizhou, transferred to Shaoxing prefecture, summoned as acting Vice Minister of Revenue, and ordered to oversee the coin foundries at Yanzhou and Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjie soon yielded the title back to Lingqin and was promoted to Secretariat drafter, served as prefect of Taizhou and then Shaoxing, was summoned as acting vice minister of revenue, and was charged with the coin foundries at Yan and Rao.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸州錢監兵匠多缺不補，積其衣糧，號三分缺額錢，令詪請以其錢付諸鹽，省朝廷銅本錢。

translations.literal: Previously, in the mints of the various prefectures many soldier-artisans were left unfilled, and their rations and clothing were accumulated under the name “three-tenths vacancy funds”; Lingjie asked that these funds be turned over to the salt monopoly to save the court its copper costs.
translations.idiomatic: Previously many soldier-craftsmen at the provincial mints had gone unreplaced, and their withheld pay and grain had piled up as so-called “three-tenths vacancy funds”; Lingjie proposed routing that money through the salt monopoly to spare the court copper costs.

sentences.zh: 又建議州縣賣官田計所入高下，守令進秩減磨勘有差；

translations.literal: He also proposed that prefectures and counties sell official fields according to the amount received, with differing reductions in merit-review time for promotion for the prefects and magistrates;
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed selling official fields by county according to revenue raised, granting magistrates and prefects graduated reductions in merit review for promotion;

sentences.zh: 州縣義倉多紅腐，請歲出三之一以易新粟；

translations.literal: in the charitable granaries of prefectures and counties much grain had rotted, and he asked that one-third be issued each year to exchange for new grain;
translations.idiomatic: where charitable granaries had spoiled much grain, he urged issuing one-third each year to exchange for fresh stores;

sentences.zh: 水旱為災，檢放不及七分處所，即許振恤：皆從之。

translations.literal: where flood or drought struck and tax relief fell short of seven-tenths, relief grain should be allowed: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: and wherever flood or drought left tax relief below seven-tenths, emergency grain should be permitted—all of which was approved.

sentences.zh: 令衿薨，令詪由崇慶軍承宣使再襲封。

translations.literal: When Lingqin died, Lingjie again inherited the enfeoffment as imperial commissioner of Chongqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingqin's death Lingjie again inherited the title, now as imperial commissioner of Chongqing army.

sentences.zh: 隆興初，除同知大宗正事，奏減生日支賜並郊祀賞給，以助軍興。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longxing he was appointed associate director of the Imperial Clan Directorate and memorialized to cut birthday stipends and suburban-sacrifice rewards to help the war effort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longxing he became associate director of the Imperial Clan Directorate and memorialized to cut birthday stipends and suburban-sacrifice rewards to support the war effort.

sentences.zh: 詔褒之。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised him by edict.

sentences.zh: 遷敷文閣直學士，特授左中大夫、知紹興府，引疾乞祠以歸，尋薨，年六十八。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture, specially appointed Left Grand Master of the Palace and prefect of Shaoxing, pleaded illness and asked for a sinecure to retire, and soon died at sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture, specially made Left Grand Master of the Palace and prefect of Shaoxing, pleaded illness for a temple sinecure, and died soon after at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 令詪蒞事明敏有風采，然在廣東日，嘗與副使章茇不協，陰中以法，陷茇於死，世以此少之。

translations.literal: Lingjie was sharp and spirited in office, yet while in Guangdong he had once clashed with Vice Commissioner Zhang Cha, secretly used the law against him, and brought Cha to his death; the world therefore thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjie handled affairs with sharp competence and presence, yet in Guangdong he had quarreled with Vice Commissioner Zhang Cha, secretly prosecuted him by law, and drove him to death—so contemporaries thought somewhat less of him.

sentences.zh: 今衿，嘉孝穆公世失子也。

translations.literal: Lingqin was a son of Shishanshi, of the line of Duke Jiaxiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqin was a son of Shishanshi, descended from Duke Jiaxiaomu of the posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 博學有能文聲，中大觀二年舍選。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, with a reputation for literary ability, he passed the palace examination in the second year of Daguan.
translations.idiomatic: Widely read and known for literary talent, he passed the palace examination in the second year of Daguan.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，為軍器少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he was Vice Director of the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingkang crisis he served as vice director of the armory.

sentences.zh: 言事忤旨，奪官。

translations.literal: He remonstrated and offended the throne, and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial offended the throne and cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，以都官員外郎召。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Shaoxing he was recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 張浚罷，令衿請對留浚，言官石公以揆論令衿阿大臣，復罷。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun was dismissed, Lingqin requested an audience to keep Jun in office; the censor Shi Gongyi impeached Lingqin for currying favor with great ministers, and he was dismissed again.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun fell from power, Lingqin sought an audience to keep him in office; Censor Shi Gongyi impeached him for fawning on senior ministers, and he was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 久之，以事抵臨安，中丞李文會劾令衿「昔為大臣緩頰，今復奔走請托。

translations.literal: After a long while, when a matter brought him to Lin'an, Censor-in-Chief Li Wenhui impeached Lingqin, saying, “In the past he spoke up for great ministers; now he is again running about soliciting favors.”
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, when business brought him to Lin'an, Censor-in-Chief Li Wenhui charged Lingqin: “He once pleaded for great ministers; now he is again lobbying and seeking favors.”

sentences.zh: 」詔送吏部。

translations.literal: An edict sent him to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the case to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 吏部直令衿，奏除德安府通判，遷知泉州。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel directly appointed Lingqin, memorialized to make him military vice-prefect of De'an, and promoted him to prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel directly appointed Lingqin, memorialized to make him military vice-prefect of De'an, then promoted him to prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 泉屬邑有隱士秦系故廬，唐相薑公輔葬邑旁，令衿建堂合祠之，郡人感其化。

translations.literal: In a subordinate county of Quan there was the former dwelling of the recluse Qin Xi, and the Tang chancellor Jiang Gongfu was buried nearby; Lingqin built a hall to worship them together, and the people of the commandery were moved by his example.
translations.idiomatic: A Quanzhou subprefecture held recluse Qin Xi's old house and Tang chancellor Jiang Gongfu's tomb nearby; Lingqin built a hall honoring both together, and local people were moved by the gesture.

sentences.zh: 歸寓三衢。

translations.literal: He returned to lodge at Sanqu.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to lodge at Sanqu.

sentences.zh: 嘗會賓客觀秦檜家廟記，口誦「君子之澤，五世而斬」之句。

translations.literal: Once, while entertaining guests, he viewed the record of Qin Hui's family temple and recited aloud the line, “A gentleman’s bounty lasts five generations, then is cut off.”
translations.idiomatic: Once at a gathering of guests he read the record of Qin Hui's ancestral temple and quoted aloud, “A gentleman’s bounty lasts five generations, then is cut off.”

sentences.zh: 通守汪召錫，檜兄婿也，頗疑令衿，諷教官莫汲訴令衿論日月無光，謗訕朝政。

translations.literal: The acting prefect Wang Zhaoxi, Hui’s brother-in-law, was much suspicious of Lingqin and prompted Instructor Mo Ji to accuse him of saying that sun and moon had lost their light and of slandering the court.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Prefect Wang Zhaoxi, Hui's brother-in-law, grew suspicious of Lingqin and induced Instructor Mo Ji to charge that he had said the sun and moon had gone dark and had slandered the government.

sentences.zh: 侍御史董德元承風旨劾之，誣以贓私。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Dong Deyuan, following the prevailing tone, impeached him and falsely charged him with corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Dong Deyuan, following the court wind, impeached him and falsely accused him of graft.

sentences.zh: 詔下令衿獄，案驗無狀，乃論令衿謗訕不遜，追一官勒停，令南外宗正司拘之。

translations.literal: An edict sent Lingqin to prison; investigation found no basis, yet he was judged guilty of slander and insubordination, stripped one rank and ordered to cease office, and detained by the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict imprisoned Lingqin; though investigation found no substance, he was still judged guilty of slander and insubordination, demoted one rank, ordered to cease office, and held by the Southern Outer Clan directorate.

sentences.zh: 檜除召錫湖南提舉以報之，銜令衿，必欲置死地。

translations.literal: Hui appointed Zhaoxi salt intendant of Hunan in return, bore a grudge against Lingqin, and was determined to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rewarded Zhaoxi with a Hunan salt intendant post, nursed a grudge against Lingqin, and was bent on destroying him.

sentences.zh: 初，趙鼎之子汾歸過衢，令衿贐之，侍御史徐嚞希檜旨，誣令衿與汾有密謀，伺朝廷機事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhao Ding’s son Fen was returning and passed through Qu, Lingqin gave him parting gifts; Supervising Censor Xu Zhe, courting Hui’s intent, falsely charged that Lingqin and Fen had a secret plot to watch court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhao Ding's son Fen passed through Qu on his way home, Lingqin gave him farewell gifts; Supervising Censor Xu Zhe, courting Hui, falsely claimed Lingqin and Fen had secretly plotted to watch state affairs.

sentences.zh: 捕汾下大理寺，俾汾自誣與張浚、李光等謀逆，而令衿預焉。

translations.literal: Fen was arrested and sent to the Court of Judicial Review, made to confess falsely that he had plotted rebellion with Zhang Jun, Li Guang, and others, with Lingqin involved as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fen was seized and sent to the Court of Judicial Review, forced to confess falsely to plotting rebellion with Zhang Jun, Li Guang, and others, with Lingqin implicated.

sentences.zh: 獄上，檜病不能省，乃獲免。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted, Hui was too ill to review it, and they thus escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was submitted Hui was too ill to review it, and they thus escaped conviction.

sentences.zh: 檜死，復爵。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Lingqin’s title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death Lingqin's rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授明州觀察使襲封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed observation commissioner of Mingzhou and inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made observation commissioner of Mingzhou and inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 引疾乞奉燕王祠，許之。

translations.literal: Pleading illness, he asked to attend the shrine of the Prince of Yan and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading illness, he asked to serve the Prince of Yan shrine and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 尋加慶遠軍承宣使。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made imperial commissioner of Qingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further made imperial commissioner of Qingyuan army.

sentences.zh: 二十八年薨，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor with Three Excellencies honors.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year and was posthumously made grand mentor with Three Excellencies honors.

sentences.zh: 秦王德芳

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Defang
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Defang

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年，詔封十王之後，以惟敘子從照封安國公，終左金吾衛大將軍、歸州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingli an edict enfeoffed descendants of the ten kings; Weixu’s son Congzhao was enfeoffed Duke of An, and ended as Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and regimental commander of Guizhou,
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qingli an edict enfeoffed descendants of the ten founding princes; Weixu's son Congzhao was made Duke of An and died as grand general of the left golden crow guard and regimental commander of Guizhou,

sentences.zh: 贈同州觀察使、齊國公。

translations.literal: posthumously made observation commissioner of Tongzhou and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: then posthumously made observation commissioner of Tongzhou and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 從照卒，以惟能子從古封安國公，終延州觀察使，贈保靜軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、楚國公，諡惠恪。

translations.literal: When Congzhao died, Weineng’s son Conggu was enfeoffed Duke of An, ended as observation commissioner of Yanzhou, and was posthumously made military commissioner of Baojing Army, Grand Councilor, and Duke of Chu, with posthumous title Huike.
translations.idiomatic: After Congzhao's death Weineng's son Conggu inherited as Duke of An, rose to observation commissioner of Yanzhou, and was posthumously made military commissioner of Baojing army, grand councilor, and Duke of Chu with the epithet Huike.

sentences.zh: 從古卒，惟憲子從式襲封舒國公。

translations.literal: When Conggu died, Weixian’s son Congshi inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Conggu died, Weixian's son Congshi inherited the title Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 惟敘字懋功，性純謹，頗好學。

translations.literal: Weixu, courtesy name Maogong, was pure and careful by nature and rather fond of study.
translations.idiomatic: Weixu, whose courtesy name was Maogong, was by nature pure and careful and rather fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，授左武衛將軍，四遷左衛將軍，領勤州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed Left Martial Guard General, was promoted four times to Left Guard General, and held the prefecture of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Duangong he became Left Martial Guard General, rose through four promotions to Left Guard General, and held Qin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，從祀汾陰，拜左千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he followed the sacrifice at Fenyin and was made Grand General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he joined the Fenyin sacrifice and was made grand general of the left thousand-ox guard.

sentences.zh: 八月，卒，年三十五。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he died, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈懷州防禦使，追封河內侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously made defense commissioner of Huaizhou and enfeoffed Marquis of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made defense commissioner of Huaizhou and enfeoffed as Marquis of Henei.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，加贈保靜軍節度觀察留後、高平郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao he was further posthumously made military administrator and observation commissioner of Baojing Army and Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao he was further posthumously made military administrator and observation commissioner of Baojing army and Duke of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 子從照，封安國公。

translations.literal: His son Congzhao was enfeoffed Duke of An.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congzhao was enfeoffed Duke of An.

sentences.zh: 從溥，至右侍禁內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Congpu reached Right Attendant of the Palace Inner Hall in the Honored Class.
translations.idiomatic: Congpu rose to Right Attendant of the Palace Inner Hall in the Honored Class.

sentences.zh: 惟憲字有則，美豐儀，少頗縱肆，長修謹，善射，好吟詠，多讀道書。

translations.literal: Weixian, courtesy name Youze, was handsome in bearing; in youth he was rather unrestrained, but grown he became careful, was skilled at archery, loved to compose verse, and read many Daoist books.
translations.idiomatic: Weixian, courtesy name Youze, was handsome in bearing; wild in youth, he grew careful, excelled at archery, loved poetry, and read widely in Daoist texts.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，授左屯衛將軍，累遷左羽林將軍、領演州刺史，加左衛大將軍、領賀州團練使，真拜資州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed Left Garrison Guard General, was repeatedly promoted to Left Forest Guard General and prefect of Yan, was made Left Guard Grand General and regimental commander of He, was truly appointed regimental commander of Zi,
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Duangong he became Left Garrison Guard General, rose to Left Forest Guard General and prefect of Yan, became Left Guard Grand General and regimental commander of He, and was formally appointed regimental commander of Zi,

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年五月卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: and in the fifth month of the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: and died in the fifth month of the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu at thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈安德軍節度使兼侍中、英國公。

translations.literal: Posthumously made military commissioner of Ande Army, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made military commissioner of Ande army, concurrent palace attendant, and Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 子從式，始封安定郡王，事見上。

translations.literal: His son Congshi was first enfeoffed Prince of Anding; his career is treated above.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congshi was first enfeoffed Prince of Anding; his career is treated above.

sentences.zh: 從演，禮賓副使。

translations.literal: Congyan was Vice Commissioner for Guests of the Court.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan served as vice commissioner for guests of the court.

sentences.zh: 從戎、從戒、從湜，並內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Congrong, Congjie, and Congshi were all Attendants of the Palace Inner Hall in the Honored Class.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong, Congjie, and Congshi all held posts as Attendants of the Palace Inner Hall in the Honored Class.

sentences.zh: 從賁，供奉官。

translations.literal: Congben was a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Congben served as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 秀王子侢

translations.literal: You, son of the Prince of Xiu
translations.idiomatic: You, son of the Prince of Xiu

sentences.zh: 子侢召赴都堂審察，改宣教郎，通判湖州，尋除直秘閣，賜五品服。

translations.literal: Ziyi was summoned to the Secretariat for examination, changed to Promulgating Instruction Gentleman, made vice-prefect of Huzhou, soon granted direct access to the Secretariat and given fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi was summoned to the Secretariat for review, promoted to Promulgating Instruction Gentleman, made vice-prefect of Huzhou, then granted direct Secretariat access and fifth-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 孝宗既封建國公，就傅，子侢召對言：「宗室之寓於外者，當聚居官舍，選尊長鈐束之。

translations.literal: After Xiaozong was enfeoffed Duke of Jian, when he took tutors Ziyi was summoned to audience and said:
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozong was enfeoffed Duke of Jian and received tutors, Ziyi was summoned to audience and said:

sentences.zh: 年未十五附入州小學，十五入大學，許依進士就舉，未出官者亦許入學聽讀，及一年，聽參選。

translations.literal: “Clansmen living abroad should dwell together in official residences, with a senior chosen to restrain them. Those under fifteen should enter the prefectural elementary school; at fifteen they enter the National University. They may take the jinshi examination; those not yet in office may also enter the university to study, and after one year may compete for selection.”
translations.idiomatic: “Clansmen posted outside the capital should live together in official quarters under a senior kinsman’s discipline. Those under fifteen should enter the prefectural elementary school; at fifteen they enter the National University. They may sit for the jinshi examination, and those not yet in office may study there as well; after one year they may enter selection.”

sentences.zh: 」高宗納其說。

translations.literal: Gaozong accepted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷朝奉郎、秘閣修撰，知處州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Court Gentleman for Meritorious Service and Secretariat Drafter, and made prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Court Gentleman for Meritorious Service and Secretariat drafter, and appointed prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而乞祠，許之。

translations.literal: Soon he asked for a sinecure and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sought a temple sinecure and was granted it.

sentences.zh: 累官左朝奉大夫。

translations.literal: He cumulatively reached Left Court Gentleman for Meritorious Service.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Left Court Gentleman for Meritorious Service.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年秋致仕，明年春，卒於秀州。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing he retired; the next spring he died in Xiu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in the autumn of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing and died the following spring in Xiu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時孝宗為普安郡王，疑所服，詔侍從、台諫議。

translations.literal: At the time Xiaozong was Prince of Pu'an and was uncertain what mourning garments to wear; an edict ordered attendant officials and remonstrance officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was then Prince of Pu'an and unsure what mourning to wear; the court ordered attendant officials and remonstrators to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 秦熺等請解官如南班故事，普安亦自請持服，許之。

translations.literal: Qin Xi and others asked that he leave office according to the Southern Court precedent; Pu'an also asked to observe mourning himself, and this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xi and others urged him to leave office under the Southern Court precedent; Pu'an himself asked to observe mourning, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 及普安建節，子侢以恩贈太子少師。

translations.literal: When Pu'an was made regional commander, Ziyi was enfeoffed by grace as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu'an was made regional commander, Ziyi was enfeoffed by grace as junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 既為太子，加贈太師、中書令，封秀王，諡安僖。

translations.literal: After he became heir apparent, Ziyi was further posthumously made Grand Mentor and Secretariat Director, enfeoffed Prince of Xiu, with posthumous title Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became heir apparent, Ziyi was further posthumously made grand mentor and director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed Prince of Xiu, with the posthumous epithet Anxi.

sentences.zh: 配張氏，封王夫人。

translations.literal: His consort was the Lady Zhang, enfeoffed Lady of the Princely House.
translations.idiomatic: His consort Lady Zhang was enfeoffed Lady of the Princely House.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，稱皇伯，園廟之制未備。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication he was styled Imperial Uncle; the regulations for the ancestral park and temple were not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne he was styled Imperial Uncle, but regulations for the princely park and temple were not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，始即湖州秀園立廟，奉神主，建祠臨安府，以藏神貌，如濮王故事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi a temple was first established at the Xiu Garden in Huzhou to receive the spirit tablet, and a shrine was built in Lin'an to house the spirit image, following the precedent of the Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi a temple was first set up at the Xiu Garden in Huzhou for his spirit tablet, and a shrine was built in Lin'an to house his portrait, following the Prince of Pu precedent.

sentences.zh: 仍班偉

translations.literal: Still ranked [text corrupt].
translations.idiomatic: Still ranked [text corrupt].

sentences.zh: 嗣秀王伯圭字禹錫，孝宗同母兄也。

translations.literal: Bogui, who succeeded as Prince of Xiu, courtesy name Yuxi, was Xiaozong’s elder brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Bogui, who succeeded as Prince of Xiu, courtesy name Yuxi, was Xiaozong’s elder uterine brother.

sentences.zh: 初，以恩補將仕郎，調秀州華亭尉，累官至浙西提刑司幹辦公事，除明州添差通判。

translations.literal: At first, through grace he entered as Awaiting Appointment Gentleman, was posted as magistrate of Huating in Xiu Prefecture, rose through offices to staff officer of the Zhexi judicial intendant, and was appointed supernumerary vice-prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered through grace as Awaiting Appointment Gentleman, served as magistrate of Huating in Xiu Prefecture, rose to staff officer under the Zhexi judicial intendant, and was appointed supernumerary vice-prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，上皇詔除集英殿修撰、知台州。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication, the Retired Emperor issued an edict appointing him Drafter of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne, the Retired Emperor ordered him made drafter of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 伯圭在郡，頗著政績，除敷文閣待制，改知明州，充沿海制置使。

translations.literal: Bogui in his prefecture achieved notable administration, was made Attendant Gentleman of the Hall for Spreading Culture, transferred to Ming Prefecture, and made coastal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In office Bogui achieved notable administration, was made attendant gentleman of the Hall for Spreading Culture, transferred to Ming Prefecture, and appointed coastal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蕃商死境內，遺貲巨萬，吏請沒入，伯圭不可，戒其徒護喪及貲以歸。

translations.literal: When a foreign merchant died within the border leaving wealth of tens of thousands, clerks asked to confiscate it; Bogui refused, and ordered his staff to escort the coffin and goods home.
translations.idiomatic: When a foreign merchant died in his jurisdiction leaving tens of thousands in goods, clerks urged confiscation; Bogui refused and ordered his staff to escort the body and property home.

sentences.zh: 升敷文閣直學士，以憂去，服闋，再知明州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture, left on mourning, and after the mourning period again governed Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture, he left on mourning; when mourning ended he governed Ming again.

sentences.zh: 新學宮，命宗子入學，閑以規矩。

translations.literal: He built a new school and ordered clansmen to enter study, instructing them in rules in his spare time.
translations.idiomatic: He built a new school, enrolled clansmen to study, and in spare moments instructed them in discipline.

sentences.zh: 詔徙戍定海兵于許浦。

translations.literal: An edict moved the garrison troops from Dinghai to Xupu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Dinghai garrison transferred to Xupu.

sentences.zh: 伯圭奏：「定海當控扼之沖，不可撤備，請摘制司軍以實其地。

translations.literal: Bogui memorialized: “Dinghai stands at a strategic choke point and must not be stripped of defense; please detach troops from the commissioner’s army to fill the post.”
translations.idiomatic: Bogui memorialized: “Dinghai lies on a vital choke point and cannot be left undefended; please detach forces from the commissioner’s command to hold the ground.”

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 海寇猖獗，伯圭遣人諭降其豪葛明，又遣明禽其党倪德。

translations.literal: Sea bandits were rampant; Bogui sent men to persuade the chieftain Ge Ming to surrender, and then sent Ming to capture his follower Ni De.
translations.idiomatic: With sea bandits rampant, Bogui sent envoys to persuade chieftain Ge Ming to surrender, then had Ming capture his follower Ni De.

sentences.zh: 二人素號桀黠，伯圭悉撫而用之，賊黨遂散。

translations.literal: The two were known as fierce and cunning, yet Bogui won them over and employed them, and the bandit bands dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Both were notoriously fierce and cunning, yet Bogui won them over and used them, and the bandit bands scattered.

sentences.zh: 以功進一官，累升顯謨閣、龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced one rank and repeatedly promoted to academician of the Hall for Illustrious Counsel and the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he advanced one rank and rose through academician of the Hall for Illustrious Counsel to the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 在郡十年，政寬和，浚湖陂，均水利，辨冤獄。

translations.literal: In ten years in the prefecture his government was mild, he dredged lake embankments, equalized waterworks, and righted wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: Across ten years in the prefecture his rule was mild: he dredged lake dikes, balanced irrigation, and cleared wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 嘗獲鑄銅者，不忍置諸法，諭令易業，民由是無再犯。

translations.literal: Once he seized men casting copper, yet could not bear to punish them by law and urged them to change trade; the people thereafter did not offend again.
translations.idiomatic: Once he caught men casting copper yet could not bear to punish them by law, urging them to change trades instead; people thereafter did not offend again.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年，授安德軍節度使，尋加開府儀同三司，充萬壽觀使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi he was appointed military commissioner of Ande Army; soon he was additionally made Grand Mentor with Three Excellencies honors and appointed commissioner of the Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunxi he was made military commissioner of Ande army; soon he was further given Three Excellencies honors as grand mentor and appointed commissioner of the Wanshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 朝德壽宮，上皇賜玉帶，加少保，封滎陽郡王。

translations.literal: When he attended at the Deshou Palace the Retired Emperor bestowed a jade belt, made him Junior Guardian, and enfeoffed him Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Attending at Deshou Palace, the Retired Emperor bestowed a jade belt, made him junior guardian, and enfeoffed him Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，入臨，充攢宮總護使，除少傅。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died he went to mourn, was appointed overall supervisor of the temporary palace, and made Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died he went to mourn, was appointed overall supervisor of the temporary palace, and was made junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，升少師。

translations.literal: When Guangzong acceded he was promoted to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong acceded he was promoted to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 逾年召見，遷太保，封嗣秀王，賜甲第于安僖祠側。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned to audience, promoted to Grand Tutor, enfeoffed heir Prince of Xiu, and granted a mansion beside the shrine of Prince Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was summoned to audience, promoted to Grand Tutor, enfeoffed heir Prince of Xiu, and granted a mansion beside the shrine of Prince Anxi.

sentences.zh: 臣僚上言：「治平中追崇濮邸，王子孫幾二十人，皆自環衛序遷其官。

translations.literal: A minister memorialized: “In the Zhiping era when the residence of Pu was posthumously honored, nearly twenty of the prince’s sons and grandsons all advanced in office from the palace guard sequence.
translations.idiomatic: A minister memorialized: “In the Zhiping era when the residence of Pu was posthumously honored, nearly twenty of the prince’s sons and grandsons all advanced in office from the palace guard sequence.

sentences.zh: 今居南班者止師夔一人，非所以強本支而固磐石也。

translations.literal: Today only Shikui among the southern rank remains—this is not how to strengthen the root branch and secure the foundation stone.
translations.idiomatic: Today only Shikui among the southern rank remains—this is not how to strengthen the root branch and secure the foundation stone.

sentences.zh: 前未建秀邸時，欲賦以祿，則不免責以吏事；

translations.literal: Before the residence of Xiu was established, if one wished to grant stipends, one could not avoid charging them with clerical duties;
translations.idiomatic: Before the residence of Xiu was established, if one wished to grant stipends, one could not avoid charging them with clerical duties;

sentences.zh: 今已建邸，而猶責吏事，他日或不免於議。

translations.literal: now that the residence is established yet they are still charged with clerical duties, someday they may not escape criticism.
translations.idiomatic: now that the residence is established yet they are still charged with clerical duties, someday they may not escape criticism.

sentences.zh: 治則傷恩，不則廢法，曷歸之南班，俾無吏責而享富貴。

translations.literal: If punished, kindness is injured; if not punished, the law is broken—how much better to assign them to the southern rank, that they may enjoy wealth and honor without clerical responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: If punished, kindness is injured; if not punished, the law is broken—how much better to assign them to the southern rank, that they may enjoy wealth and honor without clerical responsibility.

sentences.zh: 」遂詔伯圭諸子得換班。

translations.literal: ” An edict thereupon allowed Bogui’s sons to transfer to the southern rank.
translations.idiomatic: ” An edict thereupon allowed Bogui’s sons to transfer to the southern rank.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，除判大宗正事，建請別立宗學，以教宗子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxi he was appointed chief judge of the great clan directorate and memorialized to establish a separate clan school to instruct clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxi he was appointed chief judge of the great clan directorate and memorialized to establish a separate clan school to instruct clansmen.

sentences.zh: 超拜太師，免奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Grand Preceptor and exempted from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to Grand Preceptor and exempted from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 尋兼崇信軍節度使，賜第還湖州，尋薨於家。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made military commissioner of Chongxin Army, granted a mansion and returned to Huzhou, and soon died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made military commissioner of Chongxin army, granted a mansion and returned to Huzhou, and soon died at home.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝為輟朝三日，追封崇王，諡憲靖。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived the emperor suspended court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him Prince of Chong, with posthumous title Xianjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the death report arrived the emperor suspended court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him Prince of Chong, with posthumous title Xianjing.

sentences.zh: 伯圭性謙謹，不以近屬自居。

translations.literal: Bogui was modest and cautious by nature and did not put himself forward as a close kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: Bogui was modest and cautious by nature and did not put himself forward as a close kinsman.

sentences.zh: 每日見，行家人禮，雖宴私隆洽，執臣節愈恭。

translations.literal: Each day when he attended he observed family ritual; even in private feasts he was all the more respectful in ministerial demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: Each day when he attended he observed family ritual; even in private feasts he was all the more respectful in ministerial demeanor.

sentences.zh: 一日，孝宗問潛龍時事，伯圭辭曰：「臣老矣，不復能記。

translations.literal: One day Xiaozong asked about affairs of the hidden dragon period; Bogui declined, saying, “Your servant is old and can no longer remember.
translations.idiomatic: One day Xiaozong asked about affairs of the hidden dragon period; Bogui declined, saying, “Your servant is old and can no longer remember.

sentences.zh: 」問至再三，終不言。

translations.literal: ” Asked again and again to the third time, he finally said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: ” Asked again and again to the third time, he finally said nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「何太謹也。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, “How very cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, “How very cautious.

sentences.zh: 」益愛重之。

translations.literal: ” He cherished him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: ” He cherished him all the more.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲廣其居，並湖為復閣，有司既度材矣，伯圭固辭而止。

translations.literal: Once he wished to enlarge his residence and build a riverside pavilion; the officials had already measured materials, but Bogui firmly declined and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he wished to enlarge his residence and build a riverside pavilion; the officials had already measured materials, but Bogui firmly declined and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 阜陵成，遷中書令，凡五讓。

translations.literal: When the tomb of the Retired Emperor was completed he was moved to Grand Councilor; he declined five times in all.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb of the Retired Emperor was completed he was moved to Grand Councilor; he declined five times in all.

sentences.zh: 甯宗嘉其志，詔別議褒崇之禮，贈贊拜不名，肩輿至殿門。

translations.literal: Ningzong admired his resolve and ordered a separate discussion of honors; he was granted praise without naming and a sedan chair to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong admired his resolve and ordered a separate discussion of honors; he was granted praise without naming and a sedan chair to the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 子九人：師夔、師揆、師垂、師禼、師禹、師皋、師岩、師彌、師貢。

translations.literal: He had nine sons: Shikui, Shikuai, Shichui, Shixie, Shiyu, Shigao, Shiyan, Shimi, and Shigong.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons: Shikui, Shikuai, Shichui, Shixie, Shiyu, Shigao, Shiyan, Shimi, and Shigong.

sentences.zh: 師夔字汝一，初以祖恩補官，調太平州蕪湖簿。

translations.literal: Shikui, styled Ruyi, at first entered office through his grandfather’s grace and was assigned as recorder of Wuhu in Taiping prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shikui, styled Ruyi, at first entered office through his grandfather’s grace and was assigned as recorder of Wuhu in Taiping prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，改右承務郎，曆台州、秀州通判，直秘閣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he was changed to Right Assistant Gentleman, served as acting prefect of Taizhou and Xiuzhou, and was given direct access to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he was changed to Right Assistant Gentleman, served as acting prefect of Taizhou and Xiuzhou, and was given direct access to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋知徽州，新學舍，進直徽猷閣，知湖州。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Huizhou, built a new school, was promoted to direct access to the Hall for Illustrious Counsel, and governed Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Huizhou, built a new school, was promoted to direct access to the Hall for Illustrious Counsel, and governed Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 時歸附從軍而廩於湖者眾，不能給，師夔請增廩，仍別給僦屋錢，以安其心。

translations.literal: At that time many who had submitted and followed the army were rationed at Hu and could not be supplied; Shikui asked to increase rations and also separately grant rent money to settle their minds.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many who had submitted and followed the army were rationed at Hu and could not be supplied; Shikui asked to increase rations and also separately grant rent money to settle their minds.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，詔諸郡行之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it and ordered all prefectures to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it and ordered all prefectures to follow it.

sentences.zh: 除直龍圖閣，遷浙西提刑，改江東運判。

translations.literal: He was made direct access to the Hall for Dragon Diagram, promoted to judicial intendant of western Zhe, and changed to transport commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made direct access to the Hall for Dragon Diagram, promoted to judicial intendant of western Zhe, and changed to transport commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 建康務場往往奪民利，為害滋甚，師夔首罷之。

translations.literal: The service yards at Jiankang often seized the people’s profit and the harm grew ever worse; Shikui was the first to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: The service yards at Jiankang often seized the people’s profit and the harm grew ever worse; Shikui was the first to abolish them.

sentences.zh: 守臣以郡計所資，詣師夔請復舊，不從。

translations.literal: The prefect sought the circuit’s funds and asked Shikui to restore the old practice; he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect sought the circuit’s funds and asked Shikui to restore the old practice; he would not agree.

sentences.zh: 池州軍帥霍政與守臣交上書相攻，詔師夔究曲直。

translations.literal: The military commander of Chizhou, Huo Zheng, and the prefect repeatedly sent up memorials attacking each other; the court ordered Shikui to investigate right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The military commander of Chizhou, Huo Zheng, and the prefect repeatedly sent up memorials attacking each other; the court ordered Shikui to investigate right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 政密遣人求庇，師夔斥之，具言狀，政坐罷去。

translations.literal: Zheng secretly sent someone to seek protection; Shikui rebuked him, set forth the facts in full, and Zheng was dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng secretly sent someone to seek protection; Shikui rebuked him, set forth the facts in full, and Zheng was dismissed on that account.

sentences.zh: 改秘閣修撰、知明州兼沿海制置使，加敷文閣待制，轉永慶軍承宣使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Secretariat compiler and prefect of Mingzhou and concurrently coastal commissioner, made Hanlin academician of the Hall for Dispersing Culture, and promoted to imperial commissioner of Yongqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Secretariat compiler and prefect of Mingzhou and concurrently coastal commissioner, made Hanlin academician of the Hall for Dispersing Culture, and promoted to imperial commissioner of Yongqing army.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，侍父入覲，除興甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he attended his father at court and was made military commissioner of Xingning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi he attended his father at court and was made military commissioner of Xingning army.

sentences.zh: 甯宗即位，加檢校少保，充阜陵橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: When Ningzong acceded he was made acting Junior Mentor and made bridge-route relay commissioner for the tomb of the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong acceded he was made acting Junior Mentor and made bridge-route relay commissioner for the tomb of the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 阜陵成，遷開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the tomb was completed he was promoted to Honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb was completed he was promoted to Honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 侍父歸，父薨未逾月，師夔亦卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He attended his father home; not a full month after his father died Shikui also died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He attended his father home; not a full month after his father died Shikui also died, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈少師，追封新安郡王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor and enfeoffed Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor and enfeoffed Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 師揆字元輔，初補右承務郎奉祠。

translations.literal: Shikuai, styled Yuanfu, at first entered as Right Assistant Gentleman on sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Shikuai, styled Yuanfu, at first entered as Right Assistant Gentleman on sinecure.

sentences.zh: 除添差湖州簽判，改婺州通判，加直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was made supernumerary signing officer of Huzhou, changed to acting prefect of Wuzhou, and given direct access to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supernumerary signing officer of Huzhou, changed to acting prefect of Wuzhou, and given direct access to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 守臣韓元吉薦其材，上以問史浩，浩言其聰爽可任。

translations.literal: The prefect Han Yuanji recommended his talent; the emperor asked Shi Hao, and Hao said he was clever and fit for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Han Yuanji recommended his talent; the emperor asked Shi Hao, and Hao said he was clever and fit for appointment.

sentences.zh: 召對，除江東提舉。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, he was made salt commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he was made salt commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 奏免失陷常平人毋責償。

translations.literal: He memorialized to exempt persons who had lost Ever-Normal granary funds from repayment.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to exempt persons who had lost Ever-Normal granary funds from repayment.

sentences.zh: 改淮南漕，尋遷淮西提刑兼提舉，領屯田事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Huainan transport commissioner, soon promoted to judicial intendant of Huaiwest and concurrently salt commissioner, and took charge of garrison-field affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Huainan transport commissioner, soon promoted to judicial intendant of Huaiwest and concurrently salt commissioner, and took charge of garrison-field affairs.

sentences.zh: 奏以荒圩給軍士，其屯田為民世業者勿奪，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to grant abandoned marshland to soldiers, and that garrison fields that were hereditary livelihood of the people should not be seized: this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to grant abandoned marshland to soldiers, and that garrison fields that were hereditary livelihood of the people should not be seized: this was approved.

sentences.zh: 及代去，吏請獻羨錢二十萬，師揆曰：「後將病民矣。

translations.literal: When he left office the clerks asked to present surplus funds of two hundred thousand; Shikuai said, “This will harm the people hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office the clerks asked to present surplus funds of two hundred thousand; Shikuai said, “This will harm the people hereafter.

sentences.zh: 」除直秘閣，改江東轉運副使，加秘閣修撰，知明州。

translations.literal: ” He was made direct access to the Secretariat, changed to vice transport commissioner of Jiangdong, added Secretariat compiler, and made prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was made direct access to the Secretariat, changed to vice transport commissioner of Jiangdong, added Secretariat compiler, and made prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，授觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he was appointed observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi he was appointed observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甯宗即位，除奉國軍承宣使，尋升節度使。

translations.literal: When Ningzong acceded he was made imperial commissioner of Fengguo Army; soon he was promoted to military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong acceded he was made imperial commissioner of Fengguo army; soon he was promoted to military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召見，賜肩輿，超檢校太保、開府儀同三司，充萬壽觀使，襲封。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, he was granted a sedan chair, specially made acting Grand Marshal and Honorary Grand Preceptor, made commissioner of the Wanshou View, and inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he was granted a sedan chair, specially made acting Grand Marshal and Honorary Grand Preceptor, made commissioner of the Wanshou View, and inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年奉朝請，嘉定七年薨，贈太傅，追封澧王，諡恭惠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi he resumed court attendance; in the seventh year of Jiading he died, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and was enfeoffed Prince of Li with posthumous title Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaixi he resumed court attendance; in the seventh year of Jiading he died, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and was enfeoffed Prince of Li with posthumous title Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 弟師禹，由保康軍節度使除開府儀同三司，襲封。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shiyu, from military commissioner of Baokang Army, was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shiyu, from military commissioner of Baokang army, was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 十六年，薨，贈太傅，追封和王，諡端肅。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and was enfeoffed Prince of He with posthumous title Duansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and was enfeoffed Prince of He with posthumous title Duansu.
